title: Utbildningsledare
description:
Boliden är ett högteknologiskt metallföretag med egna gruvor och smältverk som arbetar långsiktigt med att garantera samhällets tillgång till bas- och ädelmetaller. I ett sekel har vårt arbete varit en del av de värdekedjor som format det moderna samhället. På Boliden vet vi att metallerna vi bryter och tillgängliggör kommer att spela en avgörande roll även framöver - det som spelar roll är hur vi framställer dem. Bli en del av oss och driv förändring för kommande generationer.

Din roll

Som Utbildningsledare arbetar du nära produktionen för att säkerställa att utbildningar och kompetensutveckling möter verksamhetens behov. Rollen handlar om att skapa goda förutsättningar för lärande och utveckling, samtidigt som du bidrar till ökad säkerhet, kvalitet och produktivitet.

Tjänsten innebär bland annat att du ska:

  • Instruera, utbilda och utvärdera nya och erfarna maskinoperatörer genom klassrums- och simulatorundervisning, samt träning på och intill maskiner.

  • Koordinera utbildnings- och träningsprogram.

  • Utforma och utveckla utbildningsmaterial.

  • Samarbeta med arbetsledning och maskinoperatörer för att identifiera utbildningsbehov och utveckla strategier för kompetensutveckling.

  • Säkerställa att maskinoperatörer har rätt kompetens och färdigheter för att kunna arbeta säkert och produktivt.

  • Coacha produktionsinstruktörer

Ditt team

Du blir en del av utbildningsorganisationen i Aitik där ni tillsammans arbetar för att utveckla kompetensen inom verksamheten. Teamet består av utbildningsledare inom både bergtruck- och lastningsverksamhet, utbildare inom autonoma system samt utbildningssamordning.

Ni samarbetar nära varandra, delar erfarenheter och stöttar varandra i det dagliga arbetet. Rollen innebär även många kontaktytor mot operatörer, arbetsledning och andra delar av verksamheten.

Ditt bidrag

För att trivas och lyckas i rollen tror vi att du motiveras av att hjälpa andra att utvecklas. Du kommunicerar tydligt och anpassar ditt budskap efter olika målgrupper, vilket gör att du skapar förståelse och engagemang i lärandesituationer. Genom att bygga förtroendefulla relationer bidrar du till ett öppet och positivt samarbetsklimat.

Du arbetar strukturerat och tar ansvar för att utbildningar och aktiviteter håller hög kvalitet, även när förutsättningarna förändras. Samtidigt har du förmågan att lyssna in olika behov och hitta lösningar som fungerar för både verksamheten och individen. Vi tror att du har ett genuint intresse för lärande och en vilja att utvecklas.

Vi söker dig som har:

  • Gymnasieutbildning, gärna med teknisk eller annan relevant inriktning

  • Tidigare erfarenhet av bergstruckarna vi hanterar i vår verksamhet

  • God datavana

  • God kommunikationsförmåga på svenska och engelska

  • Manuellt körkort för personbil

Det är meriterande om du har tidigare utbildning inom pedagogik, samt om du har erfarenhet som utbildare eller instruktör inom industrin.

Stor vikt kommer att läggas vid din personliga lämplighet för tjänsten.

Varför arbeta tillsammans med oss

På Boliden tror vi på att främja en arbetsplats där omsorg, mod och ansvar är centralt i allt vi gör. Vi erbjuder en arbetsplats där vi tror på samarbete och där det du bidrar med kommer att ha en direkt inverkan på kommande generationer. Vi är ett företag som består av ansvarsfulla och kreativa människor som alla jobbar mot samma vision; att bli den mest hållbara och respekterade metalleverantören i världen.

Ansök idag för att bli en del av något verkligt meningsfullt!

Hos oss på Boliden är mångfald och inkludering en drivkraft för innovation. Vi vet att olika perspektiv och erfarenheter stärker oss och hjälper oss att ligga i framkant i en viktig och spännande bransch. Därför uppmuntrar vi ansökningar från människor med olika bakgrunder och synsätt. Tillsammans bygger vi en arbetsplats där alla kan känna sig trygga och inspirerade att nå sin fulla potential.

Vill du veta mer om rollen? Kontakta rekryterande chef Eva-Stina Jakobsson tfn +4670-508 19 66, evastina.jakobsson@boliden.com


Frågor om ansökan besvaras av vår Talent Acquisition Partner Amanda Johansson, amanda.2.johansson@boliden.com.

Facklig information får du av
Ledarna: ledarna.aitik@boliden.com
Unionen: unionen.aitik@boliden.com
SACO: saco.aitik@boliden.com

Tjänsten är en tillsvidareanställning och skiftgående K2. Startdatum är enligt överenskommelse.

Sista ansökningsdag: Söndag 4 oktober 2026

title: Software Engineer
description:
Meet the Team

Cisco’s Enterprise IT DevOps as a Service (EDaaS) team is seeking a DevOps Engineer to assist with developing, enhancing, and maintaining, CI/CD automation supporting centrally managed DevOps tools and underlaying infrastructure, with a focus on Jenkins or GitHub Actions. EDaaS is a fast-paced group at the centre of enhancing and securing Cisco Engineering’s development workflows. To succeed in this role, you should be self-motivated and excited to be part of an innovative and continually learning DevOps team. Your demonstrated expertise in securing DevOps tools and implementing automated systems will be essential for this role.

Your Impact

  • Drive platform reliability, troubleshoot complex issues within the production environment, may serve customers through on-call rotations to identify end user problems, may lead postmortem and write root cause analysis.
  • Assist in automating infrastructure provisioning via configuration management tools
  • Apply industry accepted good practices for operational activities such as environment monitoring, deployment automation, security hardening, activity auditing, and configuration management
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams bridge the gap between software development with infrastructure operations, fostering a culture of shared responsibility for system performance, reliability, and operational excellence.
  • Managing Kubernetes clusters
  • Assist with development of automation via configuration management tools and scripts

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Systems or equivalent work experience

  • 3-4 years of recent Linux/Unix administration
  • 3-4 years of scripting experience (Python, Bash, Groovy, etc)
  • Good understanding of CI/CD workflows
  • Experience with version control systems like Git, GitHub
  • Expertise in administering and securing Enterprise Jenkins or GitHub Actions
  • Experience working with cloud platforms and Kubernetes technologies.
  • Production experience creating and using Docker images/containers
  • Experience with configuration management platforms/tools/processes, preferably Puppet or Terraform.
  • Experience generally with troubleshooting in a diverse technical environment

Preferred Qualifications

  • Familiarity with AWS including EC2, RDS, ELB, and EKS technologies
  • 2+ years of hands-on experience deploying applications to Kubernetes in a production environment, alongside two or more years of recent Linux/Unix administration, particularly with RedHat systems
  • Experience working with REST APIs
  • Leverage AI-assisted development tools and workflows to accelerate automation, enhance code quality, and streamline troubleshooting processes.
  • Preference will be given to candidates with production experience administering or applying security best practices to managed DevOps tools like Enterprise Jenkins or GitHub Actions
  • Familiar with networking (OSI layers, DNS) and reverse proxy systems (Nginx, HAProxy, Apache)
  • Solid understanding of modern software development practices and agile scrum methodologies

title: Research Analyst
description:
We are mission-driven to advance wellbeing across the Quality of Life ecosystem through impactful leadership. Come join us!

THE ROLE

The Research Analyst partners with consultants in the development, execution, and completion of search assignments and in the informational support of new business development. This role will be a thought partner and advisory to the Search teams—ensuring the research is there in support of a successful search outcome/placement.

In collaboration with business partners, the Research Analyst evaluates the work history and education of potential candidates to determine fitness and is responsible for determining the candidates who will be included in the search record. The Research Analyst will be responsible for developing a candidate identification strategy, reviewing, and analyzing research data, locating potential candidates, and assessing the highest priority candidates. In addition, the Research Analyst will retrieve and analyze relevant prior searches and use library and external resources for gathering data on potential candidates/sources/industry information.

Work will be conducted in a remote environment. This position offers a base salary of $60,000 to $70,000, plus a target bonus of 10% of base salary. Salary within our ranges is determined by your education, experience, knowledge, skills, location, and abilities, as required by the role, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. WittKieffer offers a full benefits package including medical, dental, vision, 401(k), life and disability insurances, and generous paid time off.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Research and Information Gathering:

  • Manages research projects associated with search assignments and business development, including monitoring work efforts, creating project artifacts, creating, and implementing communication plans, managing issues and risks, and reporting progress.

  • Identifies most appropriate target organizations and candidates using existing internal and external resources.

  • Seeks opportunities to develop new strategies and resources as needed.

  • Analyzes organization and candidate profiles to determine the highest priority targets for each assignment.

  • Acts as power user of the WittKieffer database.

  • Research appropriate individuals, organizations, and key industry issues to support business partners in new business development and thought leadership; presents the information in a clear format that is easily accessible.

  • Gathers compensation data for job titles from surveys, online sources or through the WittKieffer database.

  • Determine fitness of potential candidates by evaluating work history and education.

  • Conducts ongoing competitive analysis and monitoring of trade publications for new business leads.

Administrative:

  • Adds newly identified individuals to the WittKieffer database and updates existing database records.

  • Coordinates the sending of search letters with Research Operations colleagues.

  • Coordinates the placing of advertisements for open searches with Research Operations colleagues.

Foster Business Partnerships and Team Relationships:

  • Partner closely with Associates and Senior Associates within the Search solution to ensure the research is focused and supporting a successful client outcome.

  • Develops and implements a research strategy for every search, communicating regularly with the Search team on progress and/or impediments.

  • Assists other Research Analysts with overflow.

  • Actively participates in monthly research staff meetings to share resources and search strategies with the department.

  • Initiates a strategy start-up meeting with search team once a new search is booked.

  • Develops a research strategy for each search and communicates with business partners on progress.

  • Collaborate with business partners to ensure successful completion of search assignments.

  • Reviews relevant trade publications and update consultants on key topics of and changes within a given industry.

Knowledge Management:

  • Provides suggestions and input about changes to Research Strategy processes.

  • Documents the research strategies and resources used on each assignment using department standard templates.

  • Builds and documents a network of information sources (i.e., associations, publishers, suppliers, industry colleagues, etc.) to enhance internal research capabilities.

  • Contributes to the growth of the WittKieffer knowledge management repository by suggesting additional publications and developing research tools when resources do not exist.

  • Participates in Research Strategy process improvement efforts.

CANDIDATE PROFILE

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience required; advanced degree preferred.

  • 1 to 3 years' experience in executive search or similar professional services research function preferred.

Critical Competencies:

  • Strong project management skills, the ability to employ critical thinking and analysis, and proven success in creative problem solving are required.

  • Able to present and communicate information clearly and concisely to diverse audiences.

  • Must be comfortable with using reference materials, databases, social media, online services, and internet searching tools. Advanced computer skills are necessary, including proficiency with Word, PowerPoint, and Excel.

  • Excellent analytical, organizational, and customer service skills needed.

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills and the ability to interact professionally with a diverse group of people.

  • Healthcare, higher education, or not-for-profit industry knowledge acquired through education or work experience is a plus.

  • Lead and develop a high-performing team while fostering collaboration and inclusion.

  • Strong experience in strategic execution, business performance management, governance, and executive reporting.

  • Strong business, financial, operational, and analytical acumen.

  • A flexible group insurance program starting on your first day of work to meet your needs and those of your family.

title: Supplier Quality and Development Engineer (SQE/SDE))
description:
At ABB, we help industries run leaner and cleaner—and every person here makes that happen. You’ll be empowered to lead, supported to grow, and proud of the impact we create together. Join us and help run what runs the world.

This position reports to:

Quality Manager

__

Manages operational supplier quality, both on-site and off-site, ensuring the thorough execution of supplier qualification and development processes. Leads the execution of supplier Quality Wins integration, supplier assessments, and driving both corrective and preventive actions based on supplier maturity and performance levels. Manages the supplier's Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). Additionally, this role will provide leadership and support of maintaining and improving Supplier360 collaboration portal, and supplier quality processes across the ELSP NAM hub.


Responsibilities:

  • 1. Supplier Qualification and Assessment

  • Support development of Hub Level Audit Plan across the ELSP NAM hub. Ensure the execution of the supplier qualification process and that the relevant suppliers are fully qualified and remain compliant with the required standards.

  • Execute audits in coordination with local site teams and product development specialists to validate the supplier's quality and production systems and processes. Ensure completion of required supplier assessments including assessment reporting and closure of non-conformances. Verify effective closure of assessment non-conformances, by the supplier.

  • 2. Supplier product qualification and surveillance

  • Drive consistent execution of PPAP requirements to reflect the criticality of the supplier parts, materials, and manufacturing processes across the ELSP NAM hub. Lead and support approval process for supplier parts, materials, and project subcontractor services, as applicable, involving collaboration with other functions/experts, encompassing activities like Production Part Approval Process (PPAP) and product surveillance at supplier manufacturing sites.

  • Promote early supplier involvement in product development activities to maximize capture of supplier innovation and drive improvements in quality, delivery, cost, and risk management. Lead and support required product surveillance at supplier manufacturing sites to support PPAP Approvals.

  • 3. Issue resolution and claims

  • Operationally lead and support resolution of supply issues such as quality issues, late deliveries, non-conforming products or project services. For any significant issue with likely root cause supplier, support claims case and drive the PPS 8D rigor for permanent resolution.

  • 4. Supplier Quality Wins Integration

  • Develop and drive Supplier Quality Wins Integration plan for the ELSP NAM hub. Implement Quality Wins methodologies on identified suppliers to improve quality and production system capabilities and performance. Ensure plans conform to category strategies both in the short and long term. Perform Quality Wins assessments to establish a fact-based baseline of current state. This is via using standardized assessments and when necessary, build customized versions.

  • Lead Quality Wins training workshops at suppliers. Establish Kaizen plans in collaboration with the supplier team for identified development areas based on the assessments and supplier data, and carry out the action plan with necessary resources from supplier and ABB. Coach and lead team members involved in the Quality Wins activities.

  • 5. Supplier performance evaluation / monitoring

  • Maintain ELSP NAM hub level Supplier Quality metrics, including Quality Wins integration, and drive actions to meet KPI targets. Ensure full utilization of Supplier360 Reports for reporting, monitoring and disposition of quality, on time delivery (OTD) and other supplier performance metrics.

  • 6. Process and system development & utilization

  • Support & develop with ELSP NAM site functions (Sourcing, Quality, Operations, R&D / Technology), local quality procedures & practices. Ensure that locally defined systems and practices are in line with existing Division/ELSP NAM hub instructions and procedures.

  • Lead or support Supplier360 system performance, and development and enhancement of system capabilities. Note: performance and development activities may require coordination with other ELSP hubs.Ensure full and appropriate utilization of Supplier360 across the ELSP NAM hub. Provide training and ongoing support to internal ABB users and supplier users.


Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering or related technical field, with 10+ years’ experience.

  • Supplier Quality Experience: minimum 5 years’ experience in Supplier Quality, Quality Engineering, Manufacturing Quality, or a related role, with hands‑on ownership of supplier issues and corrective actions. Lean Six Sigma or ASQ certifications (CQE/CQA) are a plus.

  • Process & Continuous Improvement Mindset: Demonstrated ability to map workflows, eliminate waste, standardize processes, and drive adoption; Lean / Six Sigma experience preferred. Quality Wins experience is a plus.

  • Supplier Readiness & Corrective Action Expertise: Working knowledge of supplier qualification and audits, PPAP (or equivalent readiness processes), and structured problem‑solving methods (8D, A3, DMAIC).

  • Hands‑On, Data‑Driven Problem Solver: Proven ability to lead containment, root‑cause analysis, and corrective actions using KPIs, scorecards, and data to verify effectiveness and manage risk.

  • Technical & Cross‑Functional Collaboration: Comfortable interpreting technical requirements (drawings/specifications) and working closely with Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and suppliers to resolve quality issues.

  • Ability to travel up to 50%.

  • Fluent in Spanish, written and spoken, is a plus. Candidates must already have work authorization that would permit them to work for ABB in the US.

title: Credit Risk Officer, Energy Trading Credit Risk Management - Vice President
description:
Job Description:

Job Title Credit Risk Officer, Energy Trading Credit Risk Management

Corporate Title Vice President

Location New York

Overview

The Chief Risk Office has Group-wide responsibility for the management and control of all credit, market, operational, enterprise and liquidity risks and has the responsibility of continual development of methods for risk measurement, frameworks and creating a bank wide strong risk culture. You will work within the Credit Risk Management (CRM) area within the Chief Risk Office. CRM is a key ‘2nd Line of Defense’ function within the broader Risk Division at Deutsche Bank covering the Corporate & Investment Banks (CB & IB) along with the Private Bank.

The Energy Trading Credit Risk team is a new team that is being established to manage the credit risk arising from Deutsche Bank's expanding energy trading business. As a senior Credit Officer in the team, you will be responsible for handling approvals for all credit exposure resulting from energy trading transactions, with underlying’s covering oil, natural gas, emissions and UK and US power, you will be expected to provide expert guidance, propose risk-mitigating structures and approvals/declines, for proposed transactions, you will need to partner closely with Front Office, Market Risk, Legal and Senior CRM Management to ensure robust, forward-looking risk oversight and optimal risk/return outcomes.


What We Offer You

  • A diverse and inclusive environment that embraces change, innovation, and collaboration

  • A hybrid working model, allowing for in-office / work from home flexibility, generous vacation, personal and volunteer days

  • Employee Resource Groups support an inclusive workplace for everyone and promote community engagement

  • Competitive compensation packages including health and wellbeing benefits, retirement savings plans, parental leave, and family building benefits

  • Educational resources, matching gift and volunteer programs

What You’ll Do

  • Setting and monitoring counterparty credit limits and ratings. You will also be performing detailed credit analysis - reviewing due diligence/counterparty profiles and transaction request memos

  • Reviewing documentation terms including proposing appropriate risk-mitigation

  • Approving/declining transactions within delegated individual credit authority; and providing recommendations to Senior CRM committees/ risk approvers for larger exposures

  • Managing the end-to-end credit lifecycle of individual transactions/counterparties – including onboarding, limit setting, exposure monitoring, and early warning identification

  • Portfolio monitoring, including identification of emerging risks / trends across the portfolio, and assessment of concentration risks

  • Interfacing with senior management, business unit, internal and external regulators and other key stakeholders. You will also drive continuous improvement in processes, analytics, and reporting capabilities. Supporting digitalization/ AI initiatives in this area and supporting any internal and external audit engagement.

title: Circulation Services Clerk (Part-time, 30 hours)
description:
The Part-time Circulation Services Clerk provides extraordinary customer service to library patrons. They are often the first point of contact for library patrons and are responsible for creating a positive initial impression of the library, resolving questions and issues regarding patron accounts, and providing general information about the library. This position is responsible for the efficient and accurate circulation of library materials, which includes the checking in and out of library materials, acquiring and processing reserved items for patrons, arranging library materials on shelving carts, and shelving library materials.

The ideal candidate is a quick learner who enjoys working in a fast-paced team environment and is not afraid to make mistakes. Exceptional candidates will have strong interpersonal skills, adaptability, and an eye for detail.

About the City of Littleton

The City of Littleton is a vibrant community consistently recognized as one of America’s Best Small Cities, and a top destination for families. Discover some of the remarkable things Littleton has to offer at . With its historic and lively downtown, diverse shopping and dining options, and an extensive network of parks and trails, Littleton boasts a prime location just south of Denver and a short drive to the majestic Rocky Mountains and Colorado ski country. The City of Littleton offers excellent benefits and perks to its employees. For more details, please refer to the 2026 Benefit Guide.

This part-time position will work 30 hours per week and is eligible for benefits, which includes medical, dental, vision, and paid time off.

The City of Littleton believes in attracting and retaining the best talent and our strategies include hiring in at market pay and creating career development opportunities.

Starting pay range $19.25 - $20.30 per hour

This part-time position is non-exempt per FLSA and is eligible for overtime compensation.

Work Schedule: This part-time position will be expected to work 30 hours per week. Libraries are open late and on weekends to serve our community. This position is scheduled 4-5 days per week, including a weekend day and an evening.

Application Deadline: Applications will be accepted until finalists are identified or the position is filled, but preference will be given to complete applications received by 9/27/2026. Those who do not apply by this date may or may not be considered. In addition to your application, please submit a cover letter that describes why you are the best candidate for this position with the City of Littleton.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

Customer Service

  • Greets patrons upon their arrival at the library.

  • Checks out library materials to patrons according to established written procedures.

  • Answers phones and transfers phone calls to appropriate personnel and/or department.

  • Registers patrons for library cards by verifying identification and entering information into the integrated library system.

  • Collects fees for damaged and lost library materials from library patrons and updates balance on patron account.

  • Contacts patrons regarding damaged or missing library items.

  • Resolves problems with patron accounts and explains policies for patrons in a way that is easily understood.

Shelving

  • Ensures displays of library materials are maintained according to merchandising best practices.

  • Retrieves library materials from automated sorter bins and arranges them on appropriate carts in preparation for shelving.

  • Monitors the physical condition of the library collection by visually inspecting materials during sorting and shelving; shelves library materials; shifts collection as needed; visually scans shelved materials to maintain the integrity, continuity, and usefulness of the collection.

Circulation

  • Manually checks in library materials when needed.

  • Processes reserved items by removing expired reserved items from the hold shelf, generating daily hold reports, locating patrons’ reserved items, and shelving reserved items on the hold shelf.

  • Processes and mails overdue and billing statements.

  • Processes books for courier to deliver to other libraries.

  • Creates and processes “claims returned” and “missing item” reports and conducts searches to locate these items.

  • Assists Librarians by using pre-generated lists to remove items from shelves that are being considered for weeding.

  • Sells used books and other items for the FOLM when needed.

  • Performs other related assignments and projects as required.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  • High school diploma or equivalent; and

  • One (1) year of public library experience or two (2) years of customer service experience in a retail environment; or

  • An equivalent combination of education, training and work experience that produces the knowledge, skill, and ability to perform the essential duties and responsibilities of the position may be considered.

  • Must be able to pass a pre-employment criminal background check.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bilingual skills and ability to speak, read and/or write fluently in both English and Spanish.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES:

  • Ability to effectively and courteously communicate and interact with patrons and staff members who request information and services and deescalate situations when appropriate. Comfortable communicating professionally in-person, on the telephone, and via email. Intermediate knowledge of computer operation, intermediate skills in computer operation, experience with the Microsoft Office suite and the ability to access and retrieve needed information using the computer.

  • General knowledge of the principles of filing library materials according to the Dewey Decimal System. Intermediate/general knowledge of general library principles and procedures.

  • General knowledge of Colorado Patron Privacy law and ALA Code of Ethics.

  • General knowledge and skills using an integrated library system.

  • Ability to work as a member of a team and adapt to varying workload.

WORKING ENVIRONMENT & PHYSICAL ACTIVITIES:

  • Work for this position is performed indoors in a public building environment. This work involves exposure to dust accumulated on books and shelves.

  • Work is performed while standing, walking, and sitting.

  • Requires frequent lifting and carrying of objects weighing up to 45 pounds with or without assistance, frequent pushing and pulling of wheeled book carts weighing up to 100 pounds, working with 2-3 pound items at or above shoulder height. Also requires frequent kneeling, bending, crouching, stooping, reaching, and gripping.

MATERIAL AND EQUIPMENT DIRECTLY USED:

Personal computer with public access, on-line computer catalog, Microsoft Office 365, Sierra Integrated Library System, telephone, voicemail, automated materials sorter, electronic laser scanner, electronic cash register, DVD case locking system, photocopy machine, and wheeled book cart.

Equal Employment Opportunity

The City of Littleton is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer and intends to provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and job applicants regardless of age 40 and over, ancestry, color, disability, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information, marital status, national origin, pregnancy, race, creed, religion, sex, sexual orientation, military status, or any other status protected by applicable law, and to hire and retain the best-qualified individuals without regard to any of these factors. This prohibition includes unlawful harassment based on a protected class.

The City of Littleton will consider reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process and employment. Applicants and employees can request an accommodation by contacting Human Resources at 303-795-3857 or emailing hr@littletongov.org.

The City of Littleton is committed to the health and safety of all its employees. To ensure a safe and productive work environment the city prohibits the use, sale, dispensation, manufacture, distribution or possession of alcohol, drugs, controlled substances or drug paraphernalia on any city premises or worksites. No employee shall report to work or be at work with alcohol or with any detectable amount of prohibited drugs in the employee's system. A detectable amount refers to the standards generally used in workplace drug & alcohol testing. This prohibition specifically includes marijuana, and decriminalized psychedelics whether used for medical purposes or obtained legally under state law.

title: Assistant Editor ( Part-time)
description:
GBH enriches people's lives through programs and services that educate, inspire, and entertain, fostering citizenship and culture, the joy of learning, and the power of diverse perspectives.

At GBH, we believe in the advantages of coming together to build community, mentor and learn from colleagues, and connect more deeply with our mission. Our current hybrid approach requires staff to work onsite a minimum of two days each week, every Tuesday and Wednesday, Hybrid staff are also welcome to come in additional days each week or may be asked to come in on other days by their manager.

DEPARTMENT OVERVIEW

The Production Group provides production and post-production support to producers within and outside of GBH. The OutPost is the post-production department within The Production Group that offers on-line and off-line editing, color-grading, audio mixing and duplication/file encoding services for clients across the PBS and commercial landscape.

JOB OVERVIEW

Reporting to the Post Production Manager, the Part Time Assistant Editor (AE) supports post-production activities for OutPost and their clients. Under the guidance and supervision of the Post Production Manager and Senior Manager, the AE, will ingest and edit media, prepare assets for editors, and manage the workflows for each production. The AE will manage a wide variety of simultaneous projects that require a savvy technician who can prioritize and adapt to fast-changing environments. This is a part time position/20 hrs per week. The amount of hours may increase as the work dictates.

RESPONSIBILITIES

The Assistant editor supports productions in a multitude of ways, often with significant deadlines. This includes:

  • Support film teams in post-production by organizing media and projects, ingesting, grouping, syncing, assemblies as needed, and updating and supporting media and projects on Avid Nexus and Edit Share

  • Working with the Technology and OutPost teams: support remote workflows customized to the needs of each production and guide them through the OutPost and the GBH system

  • On-boarding producers, editors and assistant editors into GBH remote edit systems

  • Coordinating and receiving media from producers – both in physical form and through internet delivery systems.

  • Archiving and managing media and projects in coordination with on and off-site teams

  • Preparing media and sequences for editors

  • Encoding outputs of sequences and delivering them through Sony Ci and other distribution systems

  • Coordinating and assembling subtitles for translations

  • Assembling or cutting scenes from scripts

  • Additional duties as assigned

SKILL SET

  • A passion for post-production

  • A professional background demonstrating one's ability to work well under pressure, perform quickly, accurately and independently is vital for success in this position.

  • Strong organizational and communication skills and excellent follow-through.

  • Possess a calm, collegial and diplomatic disposition.

  • Proficient in Avid editing platform; knowledge of Avid Nexus, Interplay and Adobe Suite desired, including experience converting projects from Adobe to Avid or DaVinci. Knowledge of Edit Share higly preferred.

  • Experience working with several productions from end to end and be open to different modes and models of production.

  • Experience organizing and completing long-term archiving projects or media management projects is a significant plus.

  • Ability to work flexible hours, including weekend and evening work.

  • Punctuality and attendance are a must.

  • Knowledge of Macintosh and Windows, Microsoft Word, Excel and FileMaker required.

  • Organization and project management, media management, grouping, script syncing, and Avid troubleshooting skills required.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience and at least 2-3 years of experience working in production/post production environment.

This is a part time/project contract position.

This is a Local 1400 union position

description:
Michigan, United States of America


Job Family Group:

Production and Manufacturing Downstream

Regular

Experienced Professionals


Job Description:

What's the Role?

The Laboratory Technician is responsible for providing quality assurance by testing samples against established specifications and supplying customers with accurate, measured, and interpreted results. The role also involves performing routine maintenance and providing occasional repair and troubleshooting support for laboratory equipment.

The Laboratory Technician ensures that products manufactured and distributed by Shell within the envelope conform to Shell internal standards, customer requirements, and legislative regulations through strict adherence to standard quality control testing procedures.

As part of the Shell Lubricants Supply Chain team, the Laboratory Technician contributes to improving the efficiency and reliability of lubricants manufacturing, helping to enhance overall financial performance through the application of quality assurance methodologies.

The role supports Shell's lubricants business through laboratory-based testing of lubricating oils and, when required, provides product development, trialing, and investigative services to various Shell business sectors.

The Laboratory Technician is responsible for:

  • Prioritizing the safety of themselves and their coworkers above all else.

  • Performing quality control testing to ensure products conform to specifications prior to release, including:

    1. Blend oil sample testing
    2. Package filling sample testing
    3. Bulk truck/rail shipping sample testing
    4. Bulk truck/rail receiving sample testing
    5. Tank-to-tank transfer sample testing

  • Using SAP and other computerized systems to support daily operational activities and transactions.

  • Recommending updates or changes to existing formulations to optimize blend properties, where applicable.

  • Performing Blend Formulation and Laboratory functions within the SAP R/3 system.

  • Conducting trial blends of new and modified products to develop updated formulations that meet LQS standards, when requested.

  • Ensuring all lubricant oil and grease formulations remain strictly confidential.

  • Determining corrective actions for off-specification products, including up-treating, reblending, or other disposition methods, while optimizing costs and ensuring compliance with product requirements.

  • Testing, assessing, and recommending corrective actions for non-conforming products in coordination with the Quality Manager.

  • Conducting validation and calibration of laboratory equipment to ensure accurate testing results.

  • Monitoring Statistical Process Control (SPC) data for selected lubricant products to maintain LQS reduced-testing requirements.

  • Assisting the Quality Manager and Regional Area Product Manager with the development and implementation of site and regional quality initiatives and programs.

  • Troubleshooting laboratory equipment issues and test method problems.

  • Following all HSSE (Health, Safety, Security, and Environmental) guidelines in the performance of duties and responsibilities.

What we need from you

  • Must be authorized to work in the United States on a permanent basis without requiring visa sponsorship.

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.

  • Relevant post-secondary education preferred.

  • Relevant experience in a laboratory, manufacturing, quality, or related industrial environment preferred.

  • Technical skills preferred, including experience with viscosity measurement, Total Acid Number (TAN), pH testing, particle count analysis, reserve alkalinity testing, general titration techniques, FTIR (Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy), and ICP (Inductively Coupled Plasma Analysis).

  • Must possess a valid driver's license.

  • Strong problem-solving and troubleshooting skills.

  • Strong computer literacy and systems proficiency.

  • Demonstrated willingness to learn and continuously develop technical skills.

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities without compromising safety or quality standards.

  • Strong sense of urgency and accountability.

  • Ability to work effectively in a high-performance, team-based environment with a high degree of autonomous decision-making.

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

  • Ability to learn, execute, and eventually develop procedures while ensuring compliance with established standards.

  • Knowledge of ISO standards, processes, procedures, and quality management principles.

  • Familiarity with laboratory equipment operation, maintenance, and troubleshooting.

  • Experience with SAP or similar enterprise systems is considered an asset.

  • Willingness to work on a rotating shift schedule.

  • Ability to serve as a member of an emergency response team.

  • Using safe lifting techniques, must be able to lift and carry up to 20 kg from ground level to waist height.

  • Ability to work safely while wearing a respirator or Self-Contained Breathing Apparatus (SCBA).

  • Willingness to comply with Shell's drug-free and harassment-free workplace policies, as well as all safety policies and procedures.

  • Ability to work effectively in a diverse, inclusive, and team-oriented environment.

***Please note that there is an Online Assessment which is required for this position. To be considered, you must complete the assessment and receive passing score, even if you have taken previous assessments. Please review your Workday tasks, directions and instructions to ensure you complete the required test within the provided timeframe***

Overview

The Threat Intelligence function within the Chief Security Office works to proactively identify, assess, and communicate physical and cyber threats against Deutsche Bank. This position will primarily focus on physical threat intelligence across the Americas, supporting the Bank’s ability to protect its people, facilities, operations, business travelers, reputation, and overall resilience.

As the Physical Threat Intelligence Analyst, you will monitor geopolitical, regional, and local security developments and translate complex information into timely, actionable intelligence. You will collect and evaluate information from open-source reporting, intelligence vendors, professional networks, government and law enforcement contacts, and internal stakeholders. Your analysis will support executive decision-making, security operations, crisis and incident management, business continuity, and broader risk mitigation activities.

What We Offer You

  • A diverse and inclusive environment that embraces change, innovation, and collaboration

  • A hybrid working model, allowing for in-office / work from home flexibility, generous vacation, personal and volunteer days

  • Employee Resource Groups support an inclusive workplace for everyone and promote community engagement

  • Competitive compensation packages including health and wellbeing benefits, retirement savings plans, parental leave, and family building benefits

What You’ll Do

  • Define regional intelligence requirements and collect threat information from internal and external sources

  • Monitor geopolitical developments and physical threats affecting employees, facilities, travelers, and business operations

  • Analyze intelligence to assess threat probability, business impact, and recommended mitigation actions

  • Deliver risk assessments, threat profiles, alerts, reports, and executive briefings to key stakeholders

  • Provide timely intelligence support during crises, security incidents, and business continuity events

  • Collaborate with global security teams, manage intelligence vendors, and strengthen intelligence capabilities and standards

Skills You’ll Need

  • Strong knowledge of corporate intelligence, geopolitics, regional security risks, and the intelligence lifecycle

Skills That Will Help You Excel

title: Software Engineer
description:
Software Engineer, AI & Agentic AI


Meet the Team

Our team builds and runs the cloud-native services and AI capabilities that Cisco engineers, customers, and the wider developer community use every day. We take generative and agentic AI past the demo stage and into production, where reliability and security decide whether the work matters. The team pairs experienced architects with engineers who are still growing their depth, and code review here is a teaching exercise rather than a gate. You will have senior engineers close at hand, real ownership of what you build, and room to ask questions without penalty. Agentic AI is new ground for everyone, which makes this a good place to build expertise while it still counts as early.

Your Impact

Build and maintain secure microservice applications and REST APIs on AWS and Kubernetes, taking your work from requirements through testing, deployment, and support so that you own the outcome and not just the commit. Develop and integrate AI capabilities, including LLM-based features, agents, retrieval augmented generation, and tool and function calling, so that new technology reaches users as working product. Apply secure coding practice across APIs, identity, secrets, and vulnerability fixes, because a small gap early becomes an expensive problem later. Write automated unit, integration, and functional tests, and contribute to CI/CD and monitoring, so that quality holds as the platform grows. Success in this role looks like features you delivered running reliably in production, and steady growth in your depth across cloud, AI, and agentic technology.


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelors + 5 years of related experience, or Masters + 3 years of related of related experience, or equivalent related work experience.
  • 2+ years of professional software engineering experience delivering production code in one or more of Python, Java, Go, or JavaScript/TypeScript.
  • 1+ years of experience developing microservices, REST APIs, or cloud-based applications on a public cloud platform such as AWS.
  • Hands-on experience developing or deploying containerized applications in Kubernetes.
  • Hands-on experience building applications with generative AI or large language models, including exposure to retrieval augmented generation, embeddings, or tool and function calling.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning.
  • Experience developing AI-powered applications or AI agents, and familiarity with vector databases, RAG pipelines, and LLM APIs.
  • Familiarity with AI frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, or Semantic Kernel, and with Model Context Protocol or comparable AI-to-tool integration technologies.
  • Familiarity with AI security, guardrails, responsible AI, or AI governance practices.
  • Curiosity and a habit of continuous learning, with the ability to take feedback in code review and apply it, and to collaborate well across engineering, product, and security teams.

Why Cisco?

At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint.

Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere.

We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.

title: Technical Engineer, Olefins
description:
Company:

INEOS Olefins & Polymers USA

Interested in joining a winning team? A team whose employees are empowered to make a difference?

Job Title: Technical Engineer, Olefins

Job Location: Chocolate Bayou Works (CBW) in Alvin, TX

Offer Range: $104,900 - $178,570 (commensurate with experience)

Organizational Context and Job Purpose

The Olefins & Polymers USA division of INEOS is one of the largest producers of olefins and polyolefins in North America. From its manufacturing locations at Chocolate Bayou and the Battleground Manufacturing Complex, it is a merchant marketer of butadiene, ethylene, polypropylene and high-density polyethylene with annual revenue of over $4B.

The Chocolate Bayou Site is located in Southeastern Texas about 40 miles South of Houston and consists of two Olefins units that produce approximately 4bn pounds/year of ethylene, 2 Polypropylene units that produce approximately 1B pounds/ year of polypropylene, and the Light Ends storage & transfer facilities at Stratton Ridge.

How the Role Fits In

The Olefins Technical Engineer provides technical leadership for the Chocolate Bayou Olefins assets by connecting process technology expertise, optimization, capital project execution, and long-term business strategy. This role is responsible for developing technically sound solutions that improve asset capability, reduce risk, capture value, and support future business needs.

This position works closely with Operations, Business, Capital Projects, Process Safety, Reliability, Environmental, and Process Control teams to evaluate technology options, frame strategic initiatives, develop project scopes, advance optimization opportunities, preserve technical knowledge, and strengthen engineering capability across the organization.

Responsibilities and Accountabilities

Technology Stewardship
• Serve as a technical steward for olefins process technology.
• Evaluate new or modified process technologies for hazard potential, reliability implications, operability, maintainability, relief protection, environmental impact, and lifecycle value.
• Own, develop, and review process simulations, heat and material balances, equipment sizing bases, process control concepts, and safeguard requirements that support safe project design.
• Maintain awareness of industry standards, technology developments, lessons learned, and site operating constraints that influence project risk and technology choices.
• Provide technical recommendations that balance process safety, regulatory compliance, reliability, operability, energy efficiency, production capability, and economic justification.
Long-Term Strategic Business Initiatives
• Partner with Business Managers to translate long-term commercial priorities into technically sound asset strategies, project concepts, and technology roadmaps.
• Support evaluation of strategic growth, debottlenecking, feedstock flexibility, margin improvement, and market-driven initiatives by defining technical feasibility, process safety implications, and capital requirements.
• Develop early-stage technical options, risk profiles, value drivers, constraints, and trade-offs to inform business cases and long-range investment decisions.
Optimization
• Identify, develop, and support optimization opportunities that improve yield, throughput, energy efficiency, variable cost, and overall asset profitability.
• Use process data, operating limits, simulations, and technical troubleshooting to define practical improvement opportunities and quantify expected value.
• Partner with Operations, Business, Process Control, and Reliability teams to convert optimization ideas into executable actions, operating targets, control improvements, and project scopes.
• Establish sustainment measures, dashboards, or operating discipline routines to ensure realized value is maintained after implementation.
• Ensure optimization recommendations remain consistent with process safety requirements, operating envelopes, environmental constraints, and long-term asset strategy.
Capital Project Development and Execution
• Develop project objectives, technical scopes, risk-reduction cases, and business justifications that align with the plant strategic plan, long-range asset needs, business priorities, and site risk reduction objectives.
• Support development of a capital project pipeline that reflects plant SPA priorities, including process safety, environmental compliance, reliability, operability, capacity, margin improvement, and long-term asset sustainability.
• Partner with Operations, Business, Reliability, Process Safety, Environmental, and Capital Projects teams to frame project drivers, evaluate alternatives, and prioritize investments based on risk, value, timing, and execution readiness.
• Translate strategic asset priorities into clear project scope boundaries, decision criteria, technology options, implementation strategies, and measurable outcomes.
• Verify that implemented projects achieve intended risk reduction, operability, reliability, and business benefits after startup.
• Ensure Management of Change requirements are integrated into project execution plans, with clear ownership for hazard review actions, safeguard validation, procedure updates, training, and pre-startup safety review readiness.
Knowledge Management and Engineering Development
• Maintain and improve technical knowledge systems, engineering calculations, design bases, process safety documentation, and key learnings to preserve institutional knowledge.
• Coach and develop engineers and operations personnel by sharing technical reasoning, project experience, process safety expectations, and practical operating knowledge.
• Build engineering capability through structured mentoring, technical reviews, troubleshooting support, and development of repeatable tools, templates, and work processes.

• Capture learnings from projects, incidents, technology evaluations, and operating experience to improve future project quality and strengthen the technical organization.

Skills and Knowledge Required

Educational Background and Work Experience

Education

· Bachelor's degree in chemical engineering is required.

Experience

· Ten or more years of engineering experience in petrochemical, refining, chemical manufacturing, or related industries, preferred.

· Experience with continuous process operations.

· Experience in process troubleshooting and technical problem solving.

· Experience with AspenTech process simulation software.

· Experience applying process safety practices to capital projects, including PHAs, LOPAs, MOCs, PSSRs, design reviews, commissioning, and startup support.

· Experience evaluating process technology changes, design basis assumptions, safeguards, relief protection, operability, and lifecycle risk.

Preferred Experience

· Engineering experience in olefins production, including ethylene, propylene, butadiene, recovery, refrigeration, extractive distillation, reactors, and separation processes.

· Demonstrated experience supporting capital project development and execution.

This role is well suited for a technically strong engineer who can connect day-to-day asset performance, long-term strategy, capital project execution, and organizational learning into practical business impact.

title: Senior Risk Management Engineer
description:
Senior Risk Management Engineer

Closing Date: 25th September 2026 (COB)

Business Introduction
At GSK, we have bold ambitions for patients, aiming to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade. Our R&D focuses on discovering and delivering vaccines and medicines, combining our understanding of the immune system with cutting-edge technology to transform people’s lives. GSK fosters a culture ambitious for patients, accountable for impact, and committed to doing the right thing, making sure that we focus our efforts on accelerating significant assets that meet patients’ needs and have the highest probability of success. We’re uniting science, technology, and talent to get ahead of disease together.
Find out more:
Our approach to R&D

Position Summary
The Device Risk Management Lead is accountable for establishing, executing, and continuously improving risk management for medical devices and drug–device combination products across PDDS, in accordance with ISO 14971 and applicable global regulations (e.g. EU MDR 2017/745, FDA 21 CFR 820). The role provides subject-matter expertise in device risk management, owns key risk files and processes, and ensures that risk controls are appropriately identified, implemented, and verified to support safe and effective products throughout the lifecycle.

Responsibilities
This role will provide YOU the opportunity to lead key activities to progress YOUR career. These responsibilities include some of the following:
- Serve as PDDS risk owner for designated device and combination product programmes, owning the Risk Management File (RMF) and leading risk assessments (e.g. Design Risk Assessment, Use Risk Assessment, Process/Manufacturing risk assessments).
- Design and maintain risk frameworks, tools and documentation to support consistent decision making.
- Run failure mode analysis, hazard assessments and root cause investigations with cross-functional teams.
- Lead cross-functional risk assessment workshops with Human Factors, Device Engineering, Formulation, Primary Packaging, Clinical, Safety, Regulatory, Quality and Manufacturing stakeholders to identify hazards, hazardous situations, foreseeable misuse and associated harms.
- Support regulatory and audit readiness by preparing risk rationales and evidence for inspections.
- Coach and uplift site and project teams in risk thinking, tools and best practice.

Why You?

Basic Qualification
We are seeking professionals with the following required skills and qualifications to help us achieve our goals
- Degree in Engineering, Science, Risk Management, or a related discipline, or equivalent experience.
- Strong experience in risk management or reliability roles within regulated manufacturing or life sciences.
- Practical experience with ISO14971 risk methodologies such as Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA), Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) or similar.
- Strong collaborator with experience working alongside engineering, quality, operations and procurement teams.
- Clear written and verbal communication skills, able to present complex issues simply to different audiences.

Preferred Qualification
If you have the following characteristics, it would be a plus
- Experience in pharmaceutical or medical device environments with good understanding of GMP expectations.
- Formal risk or quality qualifications (for example IRCA, CQE, or equivalent training).
- Familiarity with regulatory risk expectations and inspection interactions.
- Comfortable using digital tools for data analysis, risk tracking and reporting.
- Experience coaching teams and embedding risk-led cultures across sites.
- Strong analytical and structured problem-solving skills with the ability to synthesise technical and clinical information into clear risk assessments.

Working Arrangement

This role is hybrid, with regular on-site presence required in the United Kingdom at our Ware RD site or in the US at our Upper Providence site.


What we offer
You will join a team that cares about safety, quality and the people who deliver them. You will have access to learning, mentorship and stretch opportunities. You will be part of meaningful work that connects science and technology to improve health.

How to apply
If this role speaks to you, please submit your CV and a short note that highlights your relevant experience and what you hope to achieve at GSK. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and encourage you to request any reasonable adjustments to support your application or interview. We look forward to hearing from you.


Skills

CMC Strategy, Data-Driven Decision Making, Data Integrity, Debate Moderation, Digital Fluency, GxP Regulations, Lean Management, Problem Solving, Process Optimization, Project Leadership, Risk Awareness, Scientific Writing, Technology Transfer

Why GSK?

Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together.

GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. We aim to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade, as a successful, growing company where people can thrive. We get ahead of disease by preventing and treating it with innovation in specialty medicines and vaccines. We focus on four therapeutic areas: respiratory, immunology and inflammation; oncology; HIV; and infectious diseases – to impact health at scale.

People and patients around the world count on the medicines and vaccines we make, so we’re committed to creating an environment where our people can thrive and focus on what matters most. Our culture of being ambitious for patients, accountable for impact and doing the right thing is the foundation for how, together, we deliver for patients, shareholders and our people.

GSK is an Equal Opportunity Employer. This ensures that all qualified applicants will receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, gender identity, and sexual orientation), parental status, national origin, age, disability, genetic information (including family medical history), military service or any basis prohibited under federal, state or local law.

We believe in an agile working culture for all our roles. If flexibility is important to you, we encourage you to explore with our hiring team what the opportunities are.

Should you require any adjustments to our process to assist you in demonstrating your strengths and capabilities contact us at UKRecruitment.Adjustments@gsk.com where you can also request a call.

Please note should your enquiry not relate to adjustments, we will not be able to support you through these channels. However, we have created a Recruitment FAQ guide. Click the link where you will find answers to multiple questions we receive

Important notice to Employment businesses/ Agencies

GSK does not accept referrals from employment businesses and/or employment agencies in respect of the vacancies posted on this site. All employment businesses/agencies are required to contact GSK's commercial and general procurement/human resources department to obtain prior written authorization before referring any candidates to GSK. The obtaining of prior written authorization is a condition precedent to any agreement (verbal or written) between the employment business/ agency and GSK. In the absence of such written authorization being obtained any actions undertaken by the employment business/agency shall be deemed to have been performed without the consent or contractual agreement of GSK. title: Commercial Value Leadership Lead
description:
Job Description:

The role is accountable for leading the Value Leadership and Cash agenda for Pet Nutrition and for establishing a robust, multi-year pipeline of value creation opportunities that supports the segment’s growth, margin, and cash commitments. Additionally, the role is driving cost saving transformation across segments, strengthen governance, accelerate execution, build organisational capability, and embed repeatable practices that deliver sustainable value.

  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional teams and operating seamlessly across diverse business segments and senior stakeholder groups.

  • Strategic & Commercial Acumen: Strong strategic mindset paired with commercial and financial acumen to shape and drive critical Pet Nutrition business priorities.

  • Programme Leadership: Proven ability to manage and deliver complex, high-impact business programmes from inception to completion.

  • P&L & Cash Impact: Track record of translating strategic opportunities into measurable bottom-line results, specifically P&L performance and cash flow outcomes.

  • Stakeholder Management & Influencing: Exceptional communication and influencing skills with a proven ability to build alignment and challenge senior stakeholders constructively.

  • Navigating Complexity: High comfort navigating organizational complexity, ambiguity, and dynamic priorities.

What will be your key responsibilities?

Value Leadership and Cash Delivery

  • Build and manage a high-quality pipeline of value creation opportunities in partnership with cross-functional teams, Operating Entities, and the Pet Nutrition ASPeN community. Ensure the portfolio is prioritised, governed, and progressed with sufficient pace and rigour to deliver agreed business outcomes, while representing Pet Nutrition in relevant cross-segment transformation initiatives.

Pet Nutrition Pipeline and Performance Governance

  • Lead the transition from a 12-month planning cycle to a three-year Value Leadership pipeline aligned with the 5+5 and 5S objectives. Partner with Commercial, Supply Chain, IE, R&D, Finance, RCH, and Category Heads to align priorities, targets, and delivery plans. Lead the Global Value Leadership ASPeN network to share best practices, resolve common challenges, and identify new opportunities. Manage periodic performance reviews and the annual planning and target-setting process.

  • Support Operating Entities in identifying, assessing, and shaping savings pipelines through Design to Value, cost benchmarking, and other value creation levers.

  • Lead the Global Value Leadership Big Rocks within the GTLT Simplification pillar, with clear prioritisation, governance, ownership, milestones, and delivery against strategic objectives.

Cross-Segment Leadership and Senior Stakeholder Engagement

  • Represent Pet Nutrition in cross-segment cost-saving and transformation programmes across Prime and MGS, ensuring segment priorities, requirements, and opportunities are reflected in enterprise plans.

  • Identify and accelerate scalable opportunities across segments, transferring relevant benchmarks, practices, and learnings into Pet Nutrition.

  • Partner with senior leaders across Commercial, Supply Chain, IE, R&D, Finance, and segment leadership to align priorities, resolve barriers, manage trade-offs, and secure timely decisions.

  • Establish effective governance within Commercial Pet Nutrition so that cross-segment savings translate into clear accountabilities, delivery milestones, and validated P&L impact.

  • Maintain senior-level networks and decision forums that provide transparent visibility of progress, risks, opportunities, dependencies, and required interventions.


Insights

  • Build and maintain strong external connections to stay current with evolving best practices in value delivery, including through conferences, consultants, peer companies, and other relevant external organisations. Develop performance insights and a data exchange strategy to support Value Leadership delivery, enabling better decision-making, opportunity identification, and performance tracking.


Capabilities and transformation support

  • Develop capability plans for the Value Leadership network, including change management, digital systems such as SAP, PLM, and Sievo, and financial acumen. Support major transformation programmes, including CAT and competitive complexity end-to-end supply chain initiatives, through effective deployment and execution. Champion alignment on investment priorities, increase focus on the Value Leadership agenda at key global forums such as GTLT, CLT, and S&OP+, and continue to evolve playbooks and working practices to drive value delivery, pace, and agility in service of 5+5.

What can you expect from Mars?

  • Work with diverse and talented Associates, all guided by The Five Principles.

  • Join a purpose-driven company, where we’re striving to build the world we want tomorrow, today.

  • A strong focus on learning and development support from day one, including access to our in-house Mars University.

  • An industry-competitive salary and benefits package, including a company bonus.

Mars is committed to providing access, equal opportunity, and reasonable adjustments for individuals with disabilities, long-term health conditions, or who are neurodiverse during the application and recruitment process. To request reasonable adjustments, complete our Reasonable Adjustment Request Form here.

title: Digital Producers / Sub-Editors
description:
Nine is Australia’s largest locally owned media company. We are home to premium, trusted news, sport and entertainment. Nine's assets span free-to-air television, free and paid streaming, publishing and digital audio, and digital outdoor and retail media. Our content reaches almost every Australian - meaning what we do has real impact. We bring people together, celebrate the big moments, and capture the everyday ones. As our iconic and emerging brands continue to evolve, we offer unique opportunities for you to bring fresh ideas, innovate, and make your mark on the future of Australian media.


As Australia’s most widely read masthead and number one news brand, Sydney Morning Herald is proudly committed to fearless, independent, and accurate journalism. Reaching millions each month across print and digital platforms, our newsroom offers unparalleled opportunities to contribute to a storied legacy, shape national conversations, and drive impact in the media industry.

Job Description

The Sydney Morning Herald is seeking highly motivated digital news producers and sharp-eyed sub-editors to help drive our digital-first newsroom. Working at the heart of the Herald’s fast-paced publishing desk, you will provide the final polish and presentation for Australia's market-leading journalism. Whether you are cutting through the noise as news breaks or crafting the presentation of a long-form feature, your mission is to present our stories to audiences in the most compelling way possible.

These roles (two full-time and one permanent part-time) span a dynamic roster across mornings, afternoons, evenings and weekends.

Day-to-day your role will include:

  • Quality control: Rigorously review and edit stories in our CMS, applying an intense focus on factual accuracy, grammar, syntax, and tight deadlines.

  • Audience engagement: Craft highly engaging, SEO-optimised headlines, write-offs, and captions that command attention and drive readership.

  • Digital enhancement: Elevate storytelling by expertly sourcing and integrating high-impact photographs, video, interactive graphics and multimedia assets.

  • Collaboration: Work closely with reporters, topic editors, content directors and your fellow producers.

  • Live coverage: Produce and edit live blogs, ensuring real-time copy is dynamic, engaging, and error-free.

  • Data-driven strategy: Leverage digital publishing analytics to understand audience behavior and continuously optimise story presentation.

​

What you’ll bring:

  • Proven experience in sub-editing and digital production for online publishing, and an eagerness to master new skills in a rapidly evolving digital landscape.

  • Exceptional command of the English language, grammar and syntax.

  • Flawless news judgment and an acute awareness of The Sydney Morning Herald brand and audience expectations.

  • Ability to work with speed and precision under the pressure of rolling deadlines.

  • A broad intellectual curiosity, ready to tackle topics spanning breaking news, sport, business, lifestyle and features.

  • Solid understanding of media law, specifically defamation and legal best practices.

  • An adaptable mindset with an eagerness to master new skills in a rapidly evolving digital landscape.

​

Desirable:

  • Demonstrated experience curating and editing the homepage for a major, high-traffic news masthead.

  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to make rapid, informed editorial decisions based on real-time traffic data.

  • Proven leadership capabilities in a breaking news environment, with experience directing reporters and managing desk priorities under pressure.


Additional Information

How we work
At Nine, our flexible work options vary by role and team. Depending on the position, this may include flexible hours, hybrid work, or part-time arrangements. We welcome discussing your flexibility needs during the hiring process - just ask the Talent Acquisition team.

Our employee benefits include:

Nine offers a variety of benefits and perks to support you. Learn more about our full benefits offering here:


Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion
We're committed to a safe, respectful and inclusive Nine. From day one, you'll be encouraged to bring your whole self to work and will be supported to perform at your best.


We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, people with disabilities, and of all ages, genders, nationalities, backgrounds and cultures as we recognise the importance and value of diverse perspectives. Should you require any adjustments to the recruitment process, please advise us when you apply.


Work rights: Please note to apply for this role you must already have the right to lawfully work and live in Australia.

title: Software Engineer
description:
Meet the Team

Cisco’s Enterprise IT DevOps as a Service (EDaaS) team is seeking a DevOps Engineer to assist with developing, enhancing, and maintaining, CI/CD automation supporting centrally managed DevOps tools and underlaying infrastructure, with a focus on Enterprise JFrog Artifactory. EDaaS is a fast-paced group at the center of enhancing and securing Cisco Engineering’s development workflows. To succeed in this role, you should be self-motivated and excited to be part of an innovative and continually learning DevOps team. Your demonstrated expertise in securing DevOps tools and implementing automated systems will be essential for this role.

Your Impact

  • Design, implement, and debug during software development, and supporting activities such as creating technical design documentation, feature ideation, code review, and testing
  • Drive platform reliability, troubleshoot complex issues within the production environment, may serve customers through on-call rotations to identify end user problems, may lead postmortem and write root cause analysis.
  • Implement and maintain Infrastructure as Code (IaC) to ensure environment consistency, scalability, and repeatable deployments.
  • Apply industry accepted good practices for operational activities such as environment monitoring, deployment automation, security hardening, activity auditing, and configuration management
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams bridge the gap between software development with infrastructure operations, fostering a culture of shared responsibility for system performance, reliability, and operational excellence.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Systems or equivalent work experience

  • 3-4 years of recent Linux/Unix administration
  • 3-4 years of scripting experience (Python, Bash, Groovy, etc)
  • Good understanding of CI/CD workflows and binary management for various package types, including Maven, Docker, RPM, PyPi, etc.
  • Good understanding of Github cloud, Github actions and copilot knowledge
  • Experience with version control systems, including Git and GitLFS, for managing source code (SCM)
  • Production experience creating and using Docker images/containers
  • Experience with configuration management platforms/tools/processes, preferrably Puppet.
  • Familiar with networking (OSI layers, DNS) and reverse proxy systems (Nginx, HAProxy, Apache)
  • Solid understanding of modern software development practices and agile scrum methodologies
  • Experience generally with troubleshooting in a diverse technical environment

Preferred Qualifications

  • Familiarity with AWS including EC2, RDS, ELB, and EKS technologies
  • Expertise in administering and securing Enterprise JFrog Artifactory is preferred
  • 2+ years of hands-on experience deploying applications to Kubernetes in a production environment, alongside two or more years of recent Linux/Unix administration, particularly with RedHat systems
  • Preferred Experience troubleshooting application-driven performance bottlenecks in Oracle/PostgreSQL databases to optimize query efficiency and system throughput
  • Leverage AI-assisted development tools and workflows to accelerate automation, enhance code quality, and streamline troubleshooting processes.
  • Preference will be given to candidates with production experience administering or applying security best practices to managed DevOps tools like Enterprise JFrog Artifactory, Enterprise GitHub and/or Enterprise Jenkins

Why Cisco?

At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint.

Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere.

We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.


Disclaimer

To ensure that we hire the best talent in the right way, we follow a strict hiring process and recently, Cisco has been made aware of fraudulent recruiters claiming to be from the company. Please be advised that any communication from Cisco about careers will:

  • be in direct response to an application you have submitted through the company career site

  • originate from a Cisco email address, and
  • be conducted across email, phone, or WebEx

Cisco will never make a job offer without conducting an interview process or ask you for money in any way.
