  • Serve as a key user of core HC technology platforms, including Workday and Apollo’s internal employee database system.

  • Help drive the performance management cycle, owning key components from planning through execution.

  • Partner with HCBPs and managers on the year-end compensation process, playing an active role in audits, analysis, and process management.

  • Collaborate closely with Talent Acquisition, Talent Development, and other Human Capital teams across key elements of the employee experience, including engagement, culture, training, and development.

  • Actively use and test Apollo’s internally developed HC tools, including performance management and talent development agents, and provide structured input to the HC Tech & Data team

Qualifications & Experience

  • 6-8+ years of relevant experience in Human Capital, Consulting, or other related work experience

  • Bachelor’s degree with a record of academic achievement

  • Strong analytical skill set is required

  • Experience with leveraging data to create clear and concise presentations

  • Must have advanced working knowledge with Excel, including the ability to perform calculations and automation to process large volumes of data

  • Demonstrated ability to take an idea/topic/initiative and develop a thoughtful first draft

  • Exercises good judgment and operates with the highest level of discretion and professionalism in all interactions and situations

  • Clearly communicates progress on deliverables and escalates issues in a timely manner

  • Early demonstration of business acumen and the ability to articulate, at a high level, how the business works and how their role fits into the broader organization

  • Strong demonstration of teamwork and collaboration and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment

title: Deputy Clerk
description:
Agency

Clerk of Superior Court

Division

CSC Beaufort

Job Classification Title

Deputy Clerk (S)

Position Number

65035676

Grade

JC01

About Us

DO YOUR CAREER JUSTICE! Each and every day, North Carolina's courts help provide safety for our communities, prosperity for our economy, and protection for the rights, liberties, and freedoms that sit at the foundation of our state and federal constitutions. Consider an exciting and rewarding career with us and join the more than 7,000 elected officials and employees who make up our workforce and help us ensure that justice is administrated without favor, denial, or delay.

Description of Work

SALARY RANGE: $37,404.00 - $60,502.00

The Office of the Clerk of Superior Court, Beaufort County, seeks an individual to serve in the position of Deputy Clerk, Criminal Division, in the legal system of North Carolina. Criminal Deputy Clerks perform specialized clerical and administrative work in a Clerk of Superior Court office that involves processing criminal cases. In the largest offices work may involve processing only one phase of a criminal case such as the initial filing, continuances or judgments for one or more areas of criminal district court cases (misdemeanors, infractions, and appeals from magistrate court), or superior court cases (felonies or appeals from district court). In the smallest offices work may involve processing all phases and areas of criminal cases. Work involves providing information to the public, attorneys, law enforcement, and others on criminal forms and procedures, establishing and maintaining hard copy and electronic files, and reviewing and processing documents related to assigned cases. This position requires a candidate with the ability to adapt to fast paced environments, with several different responsibilities in a focused, consistent manner while working in a high-volume office. This position will also perform tasks that involve receipting and recording payments made to the clerk of superior court. Payments received are for a wide variety of purposes, including, but not limited to, fees, fines and judgments relating to civil, criminal, estate and special proceedings. Payments receipted from the public and magistrates are typically in the form of cash. This position will also include courtroom duties.

Knowledge Skills and Abilities/Management Preferences

As a Criminal Deputy Clerk, you may perform a variety of duties such as, but not limited to, the following:

Filings

  • Discuss and explain court rules and procedures to attorneys, the public and others by phone or in person.

  • Listen and ask probing questions to determine the appropriate course of action; redirects to other departments as appropriate.

  • Identify and provide applicable forms and written instructions without providing recommendations as to any specific course of action.

Dispositions

  • Dispose of cases in ACIS/CCIS/CourtFlow; prepare probation judgments and commitments; continues cases in ACIS/CCIS; issues subpoenas; enter called and failed dates; process bond forfeitures; issue Orders for Failure to Appear (OFA) in eCourts, etc.

  • Process expunctions, orders for arrest, court-ordered bond forfeitures, fee applications, court continuances, record check requests, Civil Revocations (CVR), petitions for vehicle seizures, search warrants, extraditions, etc.

  • Audit various criminal reports; process as appropriate; prepares and sends notices to applicable parties.

Miscellaneous Responsibilities

  • Assist public, attorneys and others in conducting research of public files by pulling and re-filing case files, providing information on procedures while not offering legal advice, and making copies or assigning customers a copy-key (HECON) to make copies themselves, if requested.

  • File new and disposed criminal cases.

  • Prepare files for destruction in accordance with rules of recordkeeping.

  • Calendar cases for district and superior court.

Cashier Responsibilities

  • Process cash receipts.

  • Serve as the Clerk of Superior Court office's first point of contact for the general public and direct customers to the appropriate division.

  • Handle money daily and is responsible for their cash drawer at the end of the day.

  • Examine currency to detect counterfeit, foreign, or damaged money.

  • Record receipts to appropriate account within the Financial Cash Receipting (FCR) system.

  • Operate computer, scanner, copier, ID/Badge equipment and fax machine.

  • Sort and route incoming mail.

  • Train backup cashiers in the use of the equipment.

Some courtroom duties include:

  • Pull/Review court calendar.

  • Pull case files/shuck to prepare for court.

  • Bring required forms, pens and necessary items to courtroom.

  • Sort case files during calendar call.

  • Answer questions from attorneys, the parties involved in the cases, and the judge.

  • Start recorder, tabs and labels entries throughout the recording.

  • Administer oaths.

title: Plant Controller
description:
Imagine yourself…

  • Doing meaningful work that makes an everyday impact on the world around you.

  • Growing your expertise and expanding your skillset with every project.

  • Owning your ambition and fueling your career growth.

You have likely purchased or used a product touched by Videojet Technologies this week—after all, Videojet is a world leader in the product identification market, providing in-line printing, coding and marking products, consumables, and software solutions. Videojet’s technologies play a critical role in ensuring the safety and authenticity of products sold across the globe in the food, beverage, pharmaceutical, and industrial marketplaces.

As part of the Videojet team and the broader Veralto network, you’ll work with products that make an everyday impact on the world around you—and along the way, you’ll have opportunities to make your mark on our business and your career with ongoing opportunities to deepen your skillset and pursue your ambitions.

Learn more about how our values influence our culture and who we are;
Learn about our leading portfolio of innovative products here!


We offer:

  • A flexible, remote-friendly work environment

  • Paid holidays and a permissive paid time off policy emphasizing flexibility and trust

  • Ongoing investment in your career through dedicated training, on-the-job development, and coaching

  • Total rewards that support your success at work and beyond, including comprehensive health benefits, a 401(k) savings plan with employer match, and associate wellbeing programming with rewards

About the role:

We're seeking a Plant Controller to serve as a strategic financial business partner to the plant directors and operations leadership teams across Videojet's Wood Dale and Elk Grove facilities. In this role, you'll harness data-driven insights and deep financial acumen to identify productivity opportunities, influence operational decisions, and deliver measurable, favorable impacts to cost across North American manufacturing. This is an opportunity to sit at the intersection of finance and operations—shaping how two high-priority manufacturing sites perform financially while building your career within a globally recognized, purpose-driven organization.

You'll work closely with plant directors, cost accounting, supply chain, and the broader Operations Finance team to translate financial data into clear, actionable business intelligence. Success in this role means that within 12–18 months, the Wood Dale and Elk Grove facilities have stronger financial visibility, productivity initiatives are clearly tracked and delivering results, and plant directors view you as an indispensable strategic partner in their decision-making.

What You'll Do

In this role, you will:

  • Lead the development of site-level operating budgets and financial forecasts, collaborating with plant leadership to build credible, operations-aligned plans.
  • Partner with plant directors and site leadership teams at Wood Dale and Elk Grove to deliver proactive financial insights that drive productivity and operational decision-making.
  • Analyze plant-level cost performance, including material, labor, and overhead variances, and translate findings into clear, actionable recommendations for operations leaders.
  • Drive identification and tracking of cost improvement and productivity initiatives, ensuring financial impacts are quantified, reported, and realized.
  • Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting for both facilities, including variance analysis, KPI dashboards, and forward-looking risk and opportunity assessments.
  • Collaborate with the Cost Accounting and global finance team to ensure cost accounting practices are applied consistently and accurately at the plant level.
  • Support capital expenditure planning and post-investment analysis, partnering with plant directors to prioritize and evaluate productivity-enhancing investments.
  • Influence operational behavior by making financial data accessible and meaningful to non-finance stakeholders, fostering a culture of financial accountability on the plant floor.
  • Facilitate month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close processes for both sites, ensuring accuracy and timeliness of all plant-level financial submissions.
  • Implement and maintain strong internal controls at the site level, supporting SOX compliance and audit readiness across both facilities.
  • Partner with operations, supply chain, and business leaders to analyze inventory performance, establish inventory targets, monitor key KPI trends, and drive initiatives that improve inventory productivity, forecast accuracy, and profitability.

What We're Looking For

Minimum Qualifications

These are the must-have requirements for the role:

  • 7+ years of experience in operations finance, plant controlling, or manufacturing finance within an industrial or manufacturing environment.
  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, or a related field.
  • Proven track record of partnering with operational leaders to identify and deliver cost improvement or productivity outcomes.
  • Experience with ERP systems (SAP, Oracle, or equivalent) and strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel and financial reporting tools.
  • Demonstrated ability to synthesize complex financial data into clear, compelling business narratives for non-finance audiences.
  • Strong interpersonal and influencing skills with the ability to build trusted relationships with plant and operations leadership.

Preferred Qualifications

These are nice-to-have skills that will set candidates apart:

  • CPA, CMA, or equivalent professional accounting designation (or active pursuit).
  • Experience supporting multi-site manufacturing operations within a publicly traded company.
  • Background in standard costing, inventory management, or manufacturing variance analysis.
  • Familiarity with Lean/continuous improvement methodologies (e.g., Kaizen, VPS) and their application to financial performance management.
  • Experience with data visualization tools such as Power BI or Tableau to develop plant-level financial dashboards.
  • Prior experience collaborating across global finance teams in a matrixed organization.

Videojet is proud to part of the Product Quality & Innovation segment of Veralto (NYSE: VLTO), a $5B global leader dedicated to ensuring access to clean water, safe food and medicine, and trusted essential goods. When you join Veralto’s vibrant global network of 17,000 associates, you join a unique culture and work environment where purpose meets possibility: where the work you do has an everyday impact on the resources and essentials we all rely on, and where you’ll have valuable opportunities to deepen your skillset, pursue your ambitions, and grow your career. Together, we’re Safeguarding the World’s Most Vital Resources™—and building rewarding careers along the way.

title: Product Data Analyst
description:
Job Details:

Position Summary

The Product Data Analyst supports Tyson’s enterprise product data and digital commerce ecosystem, helping ensure products are accurately represented, discoverable, and activated across retail, foodservice, marketplace, and emerging digital channels.

This role supports product data quality, catalog health, syndication, platform operations, and governance initiatives that enable Tyson product information to scale efficiently across the business. The analyst will work across Salsify, GDSN, retailer platforms, and internal systems to maintain data accuracy, identify content and attribute gaps, monitor channel readiness, and support product content distribution to customers and partners.

This role serves as a strategic partner to Marketing, Sales, and Customer teams by enabling the accurate activation and distribution of product content across Tyson’s digital commerce ecosystem. The position helps ensure product information, assets, and content are properly structured, governed, and activated to meet customer, retailer, and channel requirements.

The role also supports workflow optimization, process automation, and adoption of data governance practices that improve the speed, consistency, and quality of product information across Tyson’s product portfolio.

This position offers a unique opportunity to develop expertise in:

  • Product Data Management (PIM/PXM)

  • Digital Shelf Operations

  • GDSN & Syndication

  • Product Data Governance

  • Workflow Automation

  • AI-Driven Product Discovery

  • Retailer & Distributor Requirements

  • Emerging Commerce Technologies

The ideal candidate is curious, analytical, detail-oriented, and eager to help scale a business-critical capability that supports Tyson’s product representation, discoverability, and activation across hundreds of customers and channels.

Product Data Quality & Governance

  • Monitor product data completeness, accuracy, and consistency across systems

  • Identify product content and attribute gaps against retailer, distributor, and channel requirements

  • Support taxonomy, attribute governance, data standards, and validation processes

  • Assist in catalog audits, data quality assessments, and remediation efforts

  • Partner with stakeholders to improve data quality at the source

  • Monitor platform health, publishing status, and system performance

  • Support configuration and continuous improvement of workflows, validations, and automation processes

  • Identify opportunities to reduce manual effort and improve scalability

Product Content & Digital Shelf Support

Reporting & Analytics

  • Develop and maintain catalog health, data quality, and operational reporting

  • Support KPI tracking for completeness, compliance, readiness, and syndication performance

  • Monitor trends and identify opportunities for operational improvement

  • Assist with dashboard development and business reporting

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Participate in process improvement and continuous optimization initiatives

  • Document workflows, business processes, and operational procedures

title: Junior Platform Software Engineer
description:
Software Engineer — Platform & Fleet Orchestrator

Develops software for the Platform Orchestrator and Fleet Orchestrator platforms with a focus on automation, reliability, scalability, security, and operational simplicity.

Builds and maintains services and automation capabilities that orchestrate cloud operations, infrastructure workflows, fleet-wide changes, and platform lifecycle activities. Applies Cisco software engineering and secure coding practices while designing solutions that are reliable, observable, maintainable, and easy for internal customers and service teams to use.

Partners with engineers, technical leads, product management, SRE/operations teams, and dependent platform teams to understand operational problems and translate them into scalable automation solutions.

Creates and maintains technical design documentation, runbooks, API and workflow documentation, and contributes to user-facing documentation required by teams consuming Platform Orchestrator and Fleet Orchestrator capabilities.

Debugs and resolves software and automation issues during development and in production environments. Participates in operational support, incident response, postmortems, and continuous reliability improvements.

Brings forward ideas for automation, simplification, platform capabilities, developer experience, and improvements to engineering and operational processes.

What You’ll Do

• Contributes to solving straightforward engineering and operational problems related to cloud orchestration, fleet management, infrastructure automation, platform services, and customer operations.

• Analyzes requirements and operational scenarios, asks questions, validates assumptions, and checks understanding before implementing solutions.

• Establishes effective working relationships within the Platform Orchestrator and Fleet Orchestrator teams and collaborates with dependent engineering and operations teams.

• Works independently or with guidance on small-to-medium features, automation workflows, APIs, integrations, or platform improvements from technical design through production delivery.

• Applies understanding of the complete software development lifecycle, including requirements analysis, technical design, implementation, automated testing, deployment, monitoring, and operational support.

• Participates in the design and implementation of distributed services, orchestration workflows, automation runbooks, APIs, event-driven integrations, and supporting platform components.

• Develops an understanding of how Platform Orchestrator and Fleet Orchestrator capabilities address operational and customer needs such as infrastructure lifecycle management, release orchestration, fleet-wide changes, maintenance activities, and automated remediation.

• Writes clean, maintainable, testable code and appropriate unit, integration, and workflow tests with guidance where required.

• Performs coding, debugging, testing, troubleshooting, and production issue analysis throughout the development lifecycle.

• Participates in code reviews, provides constructive feedback, and addresses review comments.

• Tests software and automation for reliability, scalability, performance, idempotency, failure handling, and safe execution at fleet scale.

• Applies secure coding principles and ensures solutions appropriately handle authentication, authorization, secrets, customer data, and privileged operational actions.

• Contributes to observability by implementing appropriate logging, metrics, tracing, dashboards, and alerts for owned components and workflows.

• Monitors and triages operational issues and incident reports and participates in postmortems, corrective actions, and on-call responsibilities where applicable.

• Develops deeper expertise in at least one component or capability within the Platform Orchestrator or Fleet Orchestrator ecosystem.

• Understands dependencies between orchestration services and other cloud platforms, infrastructure services, release systems, and operational tooling.

• Contributes to automation that reduces manual operational work and improves consistency, safety, and repeatability of cloud operations.

• Shares knowledge gained through development work, production incidents, technical investigations, and independent learning with the broader team.

• Creates and maintains technical documentation, including design documents, architecture decisions, runbooks, operational procedures, API documentation, and implementation notes.

• Estimates engineering assignments and communicates progress, risks, blockers, dependencies, and delays to the team.

• Identifies possible approaches to removing blockers and works with relevant teams to resolve dependencies and meet delivery commitments.

• Collaborates with engineers across teams to troubleshoot problems, share learnings, and improve common engineering and operational practices.

• Participates in continuous improvement of engineering processes, CI/CD pipelines, testing practices, deployment safety, developer experience, and platform reliability.

Minimum Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree plus 2 years of related software engineering experience, OR Master’s degree plus 0 years of related experience, or equivalent practical experience.

• Basic knowledge of software engineering principles, data structures, APIs, distributed systems, testing practices, and modern software development methodologies.

• Experience with or exposure to at least one general-purpose programming language such as Python, Go, Java, or similar.

• Basic understanding of cloud infrastructure, containers, APIs, CI/CD, or infrastructure automation concepts.

• Familiarity with Git-based development workflows, automated testing, and code review practices.

Preferred Qualifications

Preferred qualifications may vary based on specific Platform Orchestrator and Fleet Orchestrator responsibilities and business needs.

Examples include:

• Experience developing backend services, APIs, automation platforms, or distributed systems.

• Experience with Python, Go, Kubernetes, AWS, GitLab CI/CD, Terraform, or similar technologies.

• Understanding of cloud infrastructure lifecycle management and infrastructure-as-code practices.

• Experience with workflow orchestration, asynchronous processing, queues, event-driven systems, or automation frameworks.

• Familiarity with REST APIs, authentication and authorization mechanisms, service accounts, and secure secrets management.

• Understanding of reliability engineering concepts such as retries, idempotency, timeouts, failure domains, graceful degradation, and observability.

• Experience troubleshooting distributed production systems using logs, metrics, traces, and dashboards.

• Familiarity with production support, incident response, postmortems, and on-call engineering practices.

• Experience building automation used across large fleets or multiple cloud environments.

• Ability to understand operational processes and identify opportunities to replace manual procedures with safe, scalable automation.

• Strong communication and collaboration skills when working across engineering, operations, product management, and dependent service teams.

Why Cisco?

At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint.

Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere.

We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.

title: Senior Executive - Quality
description:

Role: Senior Executive Quality

About the Function:

Supply Chain & Manufacturing is where our brands are made, moved and delivered to the world.

With over half of our people working across more than 100 sites, this is a complex, large-scale operation that brings together production, logistics, engineering and supplier partnerships.

It’s fast-paced and hands-on, with teams working together to ensure quality, efficiency and sustainability at every stage. From sourcing ingredients to getting products into customers’ hands, you’ll play a role in delivering the brands people know and love.

This role is responsible for ensuring effective implementation of Quality Assurance systems across raw material receipt, production, packaging, laboratory operations, and finished product release. The position serves as a key link between shop-floor operations, laboratory activities, suppliers, and quality systems, ensuring product quality, food safety, compliance, and continuous improvement initiatives are executed effectively.

The role requires a strong understanding of FSMS, IMS, GMP, HACCP, laboratory practices, process controls, and regulatory requirements while actively supporting operational excellence and governance standards at the site.

  • Conduct trend analysis of quality parameters and drive improvement actions to enhance process capability and product consistency.
  • Utilize statistical tools for process and product quality monitoring.

Coordinate and integrate with client project teams and schedules. Lead project teams made up of both internal and external members. Maintain a broad knowledge base of industry trends as related to assigned projects.

Project management for development for new nuclear generation, including creating development plans and schedules, understanding and following Energy Northwest governance policies and procedures; coordination and integration with client project teams to ensure effective support; hiring and managing of outside technical and other consultants.

Develops the client project support plans and budgets, including tracking cost versus budget and ensuring costs and invoicing are in compliance with client contract requirements. Provide lead interface with enterprise risk management processes, including steering committees and risk review and oversight committees. Understand and maintain compliance with ERP procedures and develop and maintain necessary risk identification and mitigation documents.

Develop and manage contracts and interface with vendors. Develops project schedules commensurate with project complexity and size with the goal of being able to manage risk, accurately track projects, enforce accountability, and manage critical path and float.

Provide direction and oversight of administration and technical support assigned to projects.

Project Manager II - New Nuclear
Requires a bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in engineering, construction, project management, business, or related field and fourteen years of increasing responsibility using project management principles in a multifaceted and/or regulated industrial environment

Five years of the required experience may be in a position within the nuclear industry which includes directing project management activities and/or using project management principles.

Extensive work experience in the role of a project manager or direct supervisor in power generation/delivery, preferably within the following industries/sectors: nuclear, combined cycle, oil & gas, data centers.

Summary:

  • Attend to and care for birds in grow out houses; inspect birds to determine quality and progress by performing the below duties.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Weigh correct amounts of feed and water birds according to schedules; walk floors daily to inspect water lines, pick up and dispose of mortality, and examine birds for signs of a weak or sick bird (25%)
  • Drive farm truck to feed conversion houses to load birds ready for grow houses; transfer birds to grow out house via 4’ x 5’ door from outside Team Member to inside Team Member and place in appropriate pens (25%)
  • Calculate pen size based on bird numbers to be received and adjust to provide adequate feeder, water, and space for birds; place pen partitions according to calculations; manage floor by turning/adding shavings. Adjust controls to regulate temperature and humidity of the poultry house per instruction. (15%)
  • Sort birds by breast size (fleshing); collect weekly samples for corporate lab of cleft pallet swabs, feed, and shavings samples (25%)
  • Other duties, responsibilities, and activities may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice, such as: inspect birds to determine quality and progress by weighing birds weekly; maintenance and sanitation of breakroom, boot rooms, equipment, and vehicles; vaccinate and isolate birds to affect disease control program; administer medications to birds as needed, such as vitamins, etc.; properly euthanize weak/ill birds in accordance with company policy (10%)

Biosecurity/Animal Welfare Requirements:

  • The jobsite is a bio secure environment which requires showering, changing clothing and footwear before entering the facility. Appropriate clothing and footwear are provided by the Company. No jewelry may be worn on the jobsite except for medical ID jewelry and body piercings covered by appropriate clothing. Must be willing to sign an agreement to avoid any avian species (chickens, ducks, birds, etc.). Must be willing to sign and abide by the Company Biosecurity and Company Animal Welfare Guidelines.

Physical Demands and Work Environment:

The successful candidate(s) must be willing and able to perform the physical requirements of the job with or without reasonable accommodation.

  • Physical: Must use safe lifting techniques. Must regularly lift and/or move up to 50 pounds, items such as bags of shavings, feed buckets, bags of mortality & etc. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand majority of shift on multiple floor surfaces (i.e. concrete floor, shavings); walk; sit; use hands to handle or feel objects and controls; reach with hands and arms; balance; climbing/ladder usage; stoop/bend up to 300 times per day; talk or hear; drive a vehicle within the farm complex. Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision; distance vision; color vision; peripheral vision; depth perception; and the ability to adjust focus.
  • Environment: Required to work on wet, slippery surfaces and in hot, dry, extreme dusty, dark, wet, icy, snowy and cold environments. Low lighting conditions should be expected.
  • Personal Protective Equipment Required: Safety goggles, safety glasses, face shield, chemical gloves, waterproof apron, headlamps, and company issued footwear are required. Ear plugs will be used as required. NIOSH approved N95 particulate respirators will be worn as needed.
  • Chemicals Commonly Used: Disinfectants such as Synergize, Virocid, Lysol, hand sanitizer, Clorox wipes, bleach, etc.
  • Safety: Team member is expected to follow all applicable safety policies and procedures. These include but are not limited to Hazard Communication, Respiratory Protection, LOTO and Personal Protective Equipment. Team member is expected to identify, address and mitigate safety related risks.

title: PET/CT Technologist
description:
Akumin is a leading provider of outpatient radiology and oncology services, partnering with top hospitals and health systems nationwide to deliver advanced diagnostic imaging and exceptional patient care close to home. With a national footprint, cutting-edge technology, and a strong commitment to innovation and patient-centered care, our teams play a vital role in improving outcomes for millions of patients each year.

We’re hiring a part time PET/CT Technologist for our Porterville mobile team. This role offers the opportunity to travel and support our partner sites in Tracy and Modesto—ideal for someone who enjoys variety in their work environment.

Our PET/CT technologists use exceptional communication skills to connect with patients, explain the procedure and put them at ease. With a caring attitude and keen attention to detail, they ensure patient comfort, safety and satisfaction every step of the way. They show their technical competence by effectively interpreting physician orders/instructions and selecting appropriate software options and imaging parameters to produce the highest-quality PET/CT images/studies possible—enabling physicians to diagnose with pinpoint accuracy and treat with confidence. And, because our techs work in a variety of environments—a freestanding outpatient center, a mobile coach, or a hospital-based/inpatient facility—their flexibility allows them to deliver the absolute best imaging care at any access point.

Specific duties include, but are not limited to:

  • Responsible for patient safety including pre-screening for contraindications, aseptic injection technique, etc. and radiation safety/regulations, including proper documentation and technique when working with radioactive materials/patients.
  • Produces high quality diagnostic images
  • Effectively communicates with customers and/or radiologists

title: Retail Sunday Assistant (Blackheath)
description:
Millions of bargain-hunters. Endless pre-loved items. One meaningful purpose.

Retail store assistant (with keyholder responsibility)

£13.08 per hour + benefits

Reports to: Shop manager

Department: ​Trading​

Contract: Permanent

Hours: 6 – Sundays only

Location: Blackheath shop

External Closing date: 20 September 2026 23:55

Internal: In line with organisational policy this role will remain open for internal applications until: 20 September 2026 23:55

Please note: You must be eligible to work in the UK to apply for this vacancy. Cancer Research UK is not able to offer visa sponsorship.

​​At Cancer Research UK, we exist to beat cancer.​

​​We are professionals with purpose, beating cancer every day. But we need to go much further and much faster. That’s why we’re looking for someone talented, someone who wants to develop their skills, someone like you. ​

We’re looking for a motivated retail assistant to join Cancer Research UK’s trading team. You’ll be acting as an ambassador for Cancer Research UK and taking responsibility for the shop on a Sunday.

You’ll also be surrounded by people who are as dedicated to beating cancer as you are.

What will I be doing?

  • Overseeing the running of the shop on a Sunday. This includes taking keyholder responsibility (training provided) and supporting a talented and diverse team of volunteers.

  • Assisting the wider shop team in achieving sales and fundraising targets.

  • Reviewing and processing donated goods and new stock.

  • Coming up with creative ideas to help generate new income, with guidance from the Shop Manager.

  • Using your customer service skills to make sure our customers and supporters feel welcome and appreciated.

  • Maintaining shop standards regarding safeguarding, compliance and health and safety.

  • There will be a varied amount of manual handling and physical activity required within the day-to-day duties of the role.

What are you looking for?

  • A working knowledge of what makes great customer service.

  • Experience of working in a lively and vibrant environment.

  • Adaptability in changing situations, including being able to work effectively independently and as part of a team.

  • Commercial awareness.

  • The ability to create relationships and communicate well.

  • Flexibility, our retail teams cover the needs of their stores by working on a rota basis. Whilst a level of flexibility is needed to meet the needs of the business, we don’t forget that you have a life outside of work too.

[Download the Candidate Pack]

What will I gain?

We make sure you are supported by a generous benefits package, a wide range of career and personal development opportunities and high-quality tools, policies and processes to enable you to do your job well.

Our benefits package includes a substantial retirement plan, a generous and flexible leave allowance, discounts on anything from travel to technology, gym membership, and much more.

Our retail teams also have access to confidential wellbeing support from the Retail Trust.

How do I apply?

We operate an anonymised shortlisting process in our commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion. CVs are required for all applications; but we won’t be able to view them until we invite you for an interview. Instead, we ask you to complete the work history section of the online application form for us to be able to assess you quickly, fairly and objectively.

Owing to the nature of this position, any offer of employment for this role will be subject to a satisfactory basic DBS check.

For more information on this career opportunity please visit our website or contact us at recruitment@cancer.org.uk.

For more updates on our work and careers, follow us on: Linked In, Facebook, Instagram, X and YouTube.

Our vision is to create a charity where everyone feels like they belong, benefits from and participates in, the work we do. We actively encourage applications from people of all backgrounds and cultures, in particular those from ethnic minority backgrounds who are currently under-represented.

We want to see every candidate performing at their best throughout the job application process, interview process and whilst at work. We therefore ask you to inform us of any concerns you have or any adjustments you might need to enable this to happen. Please contact recruitment@cancer.org.uk or 020 3469 8400 as soon as possible.

Unfortunately, we are unable to recruit anyone below the age of 18, so that we can protect young people from health & safety and safeguarding risks.

title: Strategy & Planning, Lead
description:
The application window is expected to close on: 09/17/2026

Meet the Team

The GTM Strategy & Operations team for Splunk is the strategic engine behind Splunk's go-to-market motion, partnering directly with the Chief Revenue Officer (CRO) organization to shape sales strategy, planning, and executive decision-making. We translate market dynamics, business performance, and sales data into the frameworks and recommendations that guide how Splunk goes to market.

The team operates at the intersection of strategy, analytics, and operations - developing GTM frameworks, running independent analyses, and delivering executive-ready recommendations that directly influence CRO-level priorities and investment decisions.

Our team members are trusted advisors to senior leadership: independent, analytically rigorous, and comfortable owning ambiguous problems end-to-end. We value clear thinking, sharp executive communication, and a collaborative approach to solving cross-functional business challenges.

Your Impact

As the Strategy & Planning Lead on the GTM Strategy & Operations team, you will lead strategic projects supporting Splunk's CRO organization largely independently, with light guidance from your manager. You will build direct, trusted relationships with senior executives, translate ambiguous business questions into structured analyses, and develop the GTM frameworks that shape strategic decisions across the sales organization.

You bring strong analytical rigor, executive presence, and a track record of owning complex strategic work from framing through recommendation - and you're comfortable moving between deep quantitative analysis and polished executive storytelling.

● Independently lead strategic GTM projects end-to-end - from problem framing and analysis through executive-ready recommendations - requiring minimal day-to-day direction.

● Build and manage relationships with senior executives and cross-functional leaders, serving as a trusted strategic partner to the CRO organization.

● Develop and apply GTM frameworks and models to evaluate market opportunities, sales strategy options, and business performance.

● Conduct deep quantitative and qualitative analyses, synthesizing sales, pipeline, and business data into clear, actionable executive insights.

● Build and deliver polished, executive-ready presentations and business models (Excel, PowerPoint) for CRO and senior leadership reviews.

● Partner cross-functionally with sales, marketing, finance, product, and, operations to align GTM priorities and drive execution against strategic plans.

● Own analysis, reporting, and materials for recurring strategic planning cycles and executive business reviews.

Minimum Qualifications

● Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience; MBA or advanced degree preferred.

● 7+ years of experience in GTM strategy, business/sales operations, strategic planning, or management consulting.

● Advanced proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint, with demonstrated ability to build financial/business models and executive-ready presentations.

● Demonstrated ability to independently lead complex strategic initiatives from ambiguity to executive-ready recommendations.

● Strong executive presence, business writing, and communication skills, with experience presenting to senior leadership.

● Strong quantitative and analytical skills, with the ability to translate data into strategic insight.

Preferred Qualifications

● Working knowledge of SQL, Salesforce (SFDC), and/or Tableau for data extraction and analysis.

● Experience developing GTM or strategic planning frameworks used to guide executive decision-making.

● Background in management consulting, corporate strategy, or sales/business operations.

● Proven experience managing relationships with C-suite or senior executive stakeholders.

● Familiarity with Cisco/Splunk's business, sales motion, or enterprise B2B software GTM.

● Self-driven and highly proactive, with a track record of operating effectively with minimal oversight.

Why Cisco?

At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint.

Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere.

We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.

title: Director Operations Chronic
description:
PURPOSE AND SCOPE:

Acts as a serving leader to direct, administer and oversee the day to day operations and activities of dialysis facilities and programs within a specified and potentially changing geographic proximity. The scope includes, but is not limited to, chronic in-center clinics and home therapy programs, in an assigned area ensuring compliance with established company and regulatory guidelines and procedures, to provide high quality dialysis service and superior patient care to the community. Participates in the implementation of divisional and company initiatives and strategies. Practices cost containment strategies, maintaining profitability and growth of area, while ensuring compliance with all pertinent company policies and regulatory requirements.

PRINCIPAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Provides strategic leadership of short- and long-term goals through the use of thoughtful and collaborative techniques in the communication of the company’s mission and core values as a means to implement positive change and/or create organization structure within the designated facilities/programs.

Leadership

  • Acts as a serving leader to oversee the dialysis business of assigned facilities and programs within a defined area through effective leadership and management of quality patient care, customer relations, marketing and responsible fiscal management. Coordinates operational strategies and activities to ensure the provision of superior quality patient care and dialysis service while adhering to regulatory and company guidelines and requirements ensuring efficiency and economy.
  • Leads the development of area strategic plans, goals and objectives ensuring alignment with those of the region, division and company. Implements, disseminates and administers operations strategies and objectives to ensure the achievement of the division’s and company’s goals and objectives. Implements facility, program and area specific quality goals and action plans in order to achieve company quality standards.
  • Provides leadership support and guidance to facility/program management including clinical and home therapy managers and other support staff. Provides informal feedback on an ongoing basis and formal feedback in the annual performance evaluation process. Manages the staffing through the appropriate hiring, firing and disciplinary actions in collaboration with HR.
  • Mentors, guides, supports and provides subject matter expertise to direct supervisory reports with region.
  • Ensures all employees receive the appropriate training and education according to company policies and procedures including ongoing compliance training.
  • Collaborates with the appropriate Corporate and local groups to ensure the growth of all modalities.
  • Ensures a strong and robust communications process and high level of engagement between all managers and staff within the area and clinics, and across the division as needed by leading communications sessions and meetings with managers and ensuring the appropriate dissemination of communications to direct patient care and support within the area.
  • Participates in all pertinent training and development opportunities to grow and develop business knowledge, and skills and leadership competencies.

Relationships

  • Maintains continual presence in facilities and programs within assigned area and accessibility to staff and patients.
  • Acts as the primary liaison between the company and the Medical Directors, Medical Advisory Board members, and referring physicians, ensuring appropriate communication of company initiatives.
  • Responsible for developing and maintaining strong Medical Director and physician relationships.
  • Presides over facility Governing Body.

Strategic Operations/Development

  • Responsible for addressing and acting upon adverse event and action thresholds in area of responsibility.
  • Collaborates with management to develop clinical and program budgets, monitoring performance to ensure optimal, efficient and effective operations practices with regulatory and company guidelines.
    • Responsible for profit and loss management of assigned clinics, programs and areas including optimal performance of facility operations to achieve or exceed budgets and key performance indicators.
    • Works closely with Managed Care resources to increase the payor mix and to retain commercial patients.
    • Manages the payroll and oversees facility expenses and accounts payable for the assigned programs and ensures cost containment strategies are practiced.
    • Reviews the balance sheet and income statements regarding revenue growth and commercial payer mix on a frequents basis to understand the status of the business.
    • Determines impact of proposed changes and identified improvements prior to implementation to ensure a positive effect.
  • Accountable for implementing and driving the Staffing, ScheduleWise and other business initiatives including the prompt implementation of corrective action plans for clinics/programs with below threshold performance.
  • Ensures efficient and economical performance in accordance with clinic operating budgets and takes the appropriate actions to ensure the attainment of profit and year-end goals and objectives. Responsible for the implementation and achievement of the business plan and key performance indicators. Reviews analysis of performance including financial and productivity data for area with management and makes the appropriate changes in strategies, goals and objectives responding to current status and conditions. Coordinates and oversees all logistics associated with patient care within the assigned area.
  • Collaborates with the operations management team to respond to Joint Venture (JV) opportunities, to identify merger and acquisition opportunities and to participate in the related activities as appropriate. This may include, but is not limited to, providing oversight of the JV operations; participating in JV Board meetings and JV Management meetings assuming Board positions as needed, and taking the appropriate steps to ensure the JVs are in compliance with all pertinent company and regulatory requirements.
  • Maintains current knowledge regarding community and regional healthcare market and industry issues which may impact business. Utilizes current knowledge of FMCNA products, services and strategies to market the company and grow the business.
  • Works with clinical and program managers to synergize and drive patients to move to Home where applicable while balancing the needs for incenter/home programs and creating a collaborate approach.

Quality/Compliance

  • Responsible and accountable for facility/program maintenance of environmental integrity including safety of all facilities and water systems within designated area.
  • Maintains Administrative policy and procedure manuals.
  • Oversees Privacy and Security compliance according to company Risk Management and Compliance requirements.
  • Prepares reports and audits current procedures and processes to monitor efficiency of operations.
  • Practices risk management strategies and collaborates with internal and external legal counsel as appropriate to resolve legal issues with goal of reducing company exposure.

  • Performs other related duties as assigned.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORKING CONDITIONS:

The Physical demands and work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Day to day work includes desk and personal computer work and interaction with patients, facility, staff and physicians. The work environment is characteristic of a health care facility with air temperature control and moderate noise levels. May be exposed to infectious and contagious diseases/materials. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Regularly travels between locations primarily during the business day, although some out-of-the-area and overnight travel may be expected.

SUPERVISION:

Manages subordinate supervisors and/or predominately exempt staff.

EDUCATION:

  • Bachelor’s Degree; Advanced Degree preferred or an equivalent combination of education and experience

EXPERIENCE AND REQUIRED SKILLS:

  • 3-5 years of business operations management and leadership experience.
  • Demonstrated leadership and management competencies and skills including excellent financial competence, operational excellence, exceptional communication and customer service skills.
  • Strong Business Acumen; multiple modality exposure a plus
  • Demonstrated practice of continuous quality improvement and relationship development.
  • Results oriented.
  • Excellent skills for team building, motivating employees, performance management and decision making
  • Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to communicate with all levels of management through diplomacy and tact.

Fresenius Medical Care maintains a drug-free workplace in accordance with applicable federal and state laws.

Fresenius Medical Care is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, parental status, national origin, age, disability, military service, or other non-merit-based factors

40

title: Senior Project Manager
description:

title: Shift Lead
description:
Who We Are

Vireo Health of Rocky Mountain is a vertically integrated cannabis company focused on retail excellence, cultivation quality, and strategic brand partnerships across our markets. We are an organization committed to delivering an exceptional customer experience while driving disciplined, sustainable growth.

Guided by our HEART values — Hard Work (Hustle), Excellence, Attitude, Respect, and Teamwork — we operate with accountability, collaboration, and a shared commitment to performance. As we continue to scale, we are building a high-performing team ready to execute and lead in a competitive environment.

Job Title: Shift Lead

Type: Full-Time, Non-Exempt

Location: R. Greenleaf Organics | Santa Fe, New Mexico

Hourly Range: $17.00/hr with earning potential up to $22.13 per hour including tips*

Benefits Offered: Medical, Dental, Vision, STD, LTD, HSA, FSA, Dependent Care, Voluntary Life, EAP, 401(k) Match

*As a tipped industry, tips are and can be variable as a result of many factors, including shift availability, schedule, full-time/part-time status, hours of operations, weekends/nights, and specific dispensary. Our wage range is a realistic representation of the overall earnings opportunity when joining the Vireo Health of Rocky Mountain team, which includes prominent banners such as Star Buds, LivWell, and EveryDay Weed.

Position Objective

As the Shift Lead, your role is pivotal in ensuring the seamless operation of our stores, where exceptional customer service and operational efficiency intersect. You are a crucial link that aids the Store Director and Assistant Manager in maintaining a harmonious balance of adherence to policies, procedures, and operational guidelines while simultaneously enhancing the customer experience. Your contributions play a vital role in the overall success of our dispensary, making each customer visit a memorable one. The Shift Lead is a non-supervisory role, intricately woven into the fabric of our daily store operations, ensuring every aspect runs like a well-oiled machine.

Essential Functions

Customer Service (40%)

  • Provide customers with a friendly and welcoming experience, assisting them as needed.

  • Offer product information and guidance, answering questions and helping customers find suitable products.

  • Address customer inquiries and concerns, striving to ensure their satisfaction.

  • Maintain a clean and organized store environment to create an enjoyable shopping experience.

  • Collaborate with the team to suggest improvements based on customer feedback.

  • Assist with returns and exchanges, ensuring a hassle-free process for customers.

Cash Handling and Transactions (25%)

  • Support the team in training staff on proper cash handling and transaction procedures.

  • Work together with colleagues to perform daily cash reconciliation and reporting.

  • Collaborate with the finance department to enhance cash flow and financial efficiency.

  • Participate in routine cash register audits to verify accurate cash handling.

  • Assist in refining and simplifying cash handling procedures for the team.

  • Help colleagues with advanced cash register functionalities for smoother transactions.

Inventory Management (15%)

  • Contribute to maintaining product quality and safety standards.

  • Support the organization of products for easy restocking and accessibility.

  • Collaborate with the inventory management team to ensure accurate inventory levels.

  • Assist in implementing in-store promotions and sales strategies to manage inventory.

  • Participate in monitoring supply chain performance and identifying process improvement opportunities.

  • Collaborate with team members to report and analyze product trends and customer preferences.

Please note that the percentage allocations are a general estimate and may vary based on business needs and priorities. Additional duties may be required as needed to support overall operations.

Requirements

Education and Experience

  • High school diploma or equivalent preferred.

  • Must be at least 21 years of age.

  • Previous experience in a retail or customer service role is preferred.

  • Knowledge of cannabis and its products is a plus.

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.

  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment.

  • Proficient in cash handling and accurate basic math calculations.

  • Reliable, punctual, and possesses a strong work ethic.

Working Conditions (Schedule, Environment, Travel)

  • Ability to lift 25 lbs. or more multiple times per day.

  • Stores are open 7 days a week from 8:00 am – 11:45 pm (varying by location), nights, weekends & holidays.

  • The schedule will vary depending on the needs of the business.

  • Must be able to obtain and maintain a valid New Mexico Food Handler License to support safe and compliant handling of cannabis products.

Why Choose Vireo?
Life’s too short to work somewhere that doesn’t ignite your passion. The cannabis industry is fast-paced, innovative, and full of opportunity—where science meets creativity, and wellness meets culture.

At Vireo Health, we’re pioneering the future of cannabis with a team that’s as dynamic as the industry itself. Here, you’ll find a workplace that’s collaborative, inclusive, and driven by HEART and purpose, where your work has a real impact on people’s lives.

Whether you’re cultivating the highest-quality plants, crafting cutting-edge products, or shaping unforgettable customer experiences, you’ll be part of something bigger. If you’re looking for a career that’s exciting, meaningful, and full of growth, let’s build the future of cannabis together.

✅ A Growing Industry: Work at the leading tech company in the cannabis industry and help shape the future
✅ Passionate Culture: Join a team that truly cares about the plant, the people, and the purpose behind what we do
✅ Employee Perks: Enjoy competitive pay and employee discounts
✅ Making an Impact: We’re committed to education, sustainability, and giving back to the communities we serve.

EEO Statement
Vireo Health, Inc. is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

To be considered for this position your application must be submitted by August 18th, 2026. If after said date the position is not filled, applications will be accepted until the position is filled.

title: Senior/EHS Engineer
description:
This position is a contract role and its tenure will be until 30 December 2028.

Purpose

Oversee site Security, Safety, Health, and Environmental programs to ensure compliance with legislation and GSK EHS standards for a safe workplace. Drive continuous improvement, best practices, and a strong EHS culture. Provide technical guidance, training, and support to the business.


Responsibilities

  • EHS Management system – Maintain site’s EHS management system to ensure compliance with legal and GSK EHS standards requirements while also facilitating continuous improvement. This include ensuring effective risk management and risk assessments.
  • EHS Strategies and Plans – Contribute to the development of site’s EHS strategies, plans, policies, procedures and risk assessment techniques. Support implementation of GSK life-saving rules, safe systems of work, and behavioural safety programmes.
  • EHS Information, Guidance and Advice – Ensure site complies with all relevant aspect concerning safety, industrial hygiene and environmental protection as prescribed by corporate EHS standards, Engineering Standards and local statutory requirements. Monitor changes in corporate EHS standards and local requirements and ensure site procedures are reviewed and updated to comply with the new requirements. Enforce EHS requirements and procedures and ensure that these are followed by all staffs and contractors working on site.
  • Training – Create and deliver EHS packages and train staff and contractors at various levels within the organization. Identify EHS training needs and providers through in-house or external resources.
  • Audit – Develop and support management monitoring (self-inspection, gemba) and conduct regular independent business monitoring of the EHS management systems and controls. Coordinate and follow up on matters arising from all EHS audits and inspections. Leads and coaches the SEHS committee’s inspection teams in regular site EHS inspections.
  • Responding to Problems – Report accidents, illnesses or other incidents to the relevant authorities and departments where required. Together with the relevant departments, facilitate the investigation of any accidents and dangerous occurrences and ensure recommendations are effective to prevent their recurrence.
  • Communications – Reinforce site’s safety culture via activities and campaigns to promote and enhance awareness of staffs and contractors.
  • Support the EHS Lead, other EHS team members to ensure that EHS is maintained to a high standard on site.

Key Requirements:

  • Minimum Bachelor’s degree from an accredited university in EHS, Industrial Hygiene, Engineering or Science related field
  • Minimum 2 years of experience in pharmaceutical, chemical or other high-risk manufacturing facilities
  • Ability to provide confidence to stakeholders and to provide sounds, practical EHS advice to the business and reliable decision-making.

How to apply
If this role aligns with your experience and goals, we want to hear from you. Please apply and tell us how you will contribute to a safer, more sustainable workplace and grow your EHS career at GSK.


Skills

Data-Driven Decision Making, Data Integrity, Digital Fluency, GxP Regulations, Incident Investigations, Influencing Without Authority, Lean Management, Problem Solving, Regulatory Compliance, Risk Assessments, Risk Awareness

Why GSK?

Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together.

GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. We aim to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade, as a successful, growing company where people can thrive. We get ahead of disease by preventing and treating it with innovation in specialty medicines and vaccines. We focus on four therapeutic areas: respiratory, immunology and inflammation; oncology; HIV; and infectious diseases – to impact health at scale.

People and patients around the world count on the medicines and vaccines we make, so we’re committed to creating an environment where our people can thrive and focus on what matters most. Our culture of being ambitious for patients, accountable for impact and doing the right thing is the foundation for how, together, we deliver for patients, shareholders and our people.

title: Senior Hardware Design Engineer
description:

This role requires the employee to work onsite at the Austin, TX office location.

Meet the Team

The Common Hardware Group (CHG) creates innovative hardware platforms central to the AI era, powering Cisco’s core Switching, Routing, and Wireless products for organizations globally. Our innovations in silicon, optics, and hardware platforms—like Silicon One—are shaping the technology industry.

The Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series hardware team within CHG is responsible for designing and developing the stackable enterprise switching platform tailored for security, mobility, and cloud applications. This role directly impacts Cisco’s Catalyst switching business by delivering reliable, scalable, and cost-effective hardware platforms for enterprise campus networks. The engineer will contribute across design, validation, manufacturing, and sustaining activities, with influence on product quality, customer experience, supply continuity, and Cisco’s competitive position in enterprise networking.

  • Drives technical execution across hardware design, validation, bring-up, diagnostics, compliance, manufacturing readiness, and sustaining support.

  • Influences product cost, manufacturability, supply continuity, and lifecycle efficiency through strong engineering decisions.

  • Partner with software, mechanical, signal integrity, power, thermal, manufacturing, supply chain, compliance, product management, and customer support teams.

  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical or computer engineering + 7 years of related experience OR master’s degree in electrical or computer Engineering + 4 years of related experience.

  • Experience in hardware design, validation, bring-up, and debug for complex electronic systems.

  • Experience with lab equipment such as Oscilloscopes, Logic Analyzers, Function generators, protocol analyzers, etc.

Preferred Qualifications:

At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. Job Summary: The Laboratory Coordinator is responsible for supporting laboratory operations through specimen intake, administrative duties, data entry, transcription, and general lab maintenance. This role does not involve performing technical laboratory duties but is critical to maintaining the efficiency of lab processes. The Lab Coordinator is expected to adhere to all Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) with attention to detail, accuracy, professionalism, and a strong commitment to compliance and safety.

Schedule: Full Time, 30+ hours. Monday to Friday 7:30am – 4:00pm.

Laboratory Coordinator:

  • Receive laboratory specimens from couriers.
  • Review specimens for proper labeling and acceptability.
  • Resolve labeling discrepancies according to SOPs.
  • Sort specimens for in-house processing or send-outs based on insurance coverage, provider preference, and case type.
  • Accession specimens into the Laboratory Information System (LIS).
  • Prepare cases for scanning including performing quality control checks. Then scanning specimens into the LIS.
  • Prepare cases for reference laboratories and confirm daily pickups.
  • Dispose of biohazard and hazardous waste in accordance with policies and regulations.
  • Maintain a safe and clean work environment, adhering to all OSHA, CLIA, and company-specific protocols.
  • Lab Coordinator is responsible for assisting in all customer inquiries related to but not limited to:
  • Assist with inquiries related to:
  • Missing or delayed pathology reports.
  • Modifications to orders, requisitions, or reports.
  • Requests for slides or blocks for consultations and second opinions.
  • Investigate and resolve lab-related inquiries, including cases processed both internally and at reference laboratories that come in the form of phone calls, voicemail, ModMed/EMA tasks, email and support tickets (via Fresh Desk)
  • Provide data entry support to Pathologist(s).
  • The Lab Coordinator will receive diagnostic codes and/or additional test orders from the pathologist.
  • Codes and orders will be shared by the pathologist either verbally or handwritten on pathology requisitions.
  • The Lab Coordinator will enter the orders into the LIS for the other team members to access and process.
  • The Lab Coordinator will enter the diagnostic code(s) and associated billing code(s) into the LIS to produce a macro, a paragraph of diagnostic information.
  • The Lab Coordinator will close the case which will add the case to the queue for the pathologist to sign-out.

General Laboratory Duties:

  • File and retrieve histology slides and paraffin blocks following laboratory protocols.
  • Maintain an organized filing system for easy access and retrieval.
  • Assist with archiving and tracking slide and block locations.
  • Keep workstations, lab benches, and equipment clean and organized.
  • Dispose of biohazard waste properly and restock cleaning supplies.
  • Clean and disinfect lab equipment and ensure compliance with safety regulations.
  • Maintain inventory, restock lab supplies, and put away shipments upon arrival.
  • Assist in audits, quality control (QC), and compliance-related tasks as needed.

Qualifications:

  • High School Diploma/GED minimum required; Associate degree preferred
  • Must be computer savvy and familiar with Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook with strong communication, interpersonal, and organizational skills with six months experience in a similar role.
  • Training and a post training assessment for all role-applicable SOPs and Laboratory Compliance workflows must be completed after hire but before any laboratory work can be completed independently. A competency assessment will occur at one month before independent work is permitted. Role specific SOPs and Laboratory Compliance workflows are outlined in the Pathology Training Program Smartsheet.
  • Employee is expected to be in their office(s) during the week. Employee may be expected to travel up to 25% or less of their time from their home office. Other travel outside of their region and/or to the corporate office may be needed from time to time.

This role is based in Glen Carbon, IL

description:
Wood Mackenzie is the global leader in analytics, insights and proprietary data across the entire energy and natural resources landscape.


For over 50 years our work has guided the decisions of the world’s most influential energy producers, utilities companies, financial institutions and governments.


Now, with the world’s energy system more complex and interconnected than ever before, sector-specific views are no longer enough. That’s why we’ve redefined what’s possible with Intelligence Connected.


By fusing our unparalleled proprietary data with the sharpest analytical minds, all supercharged by Synoptic AI, we deliver a clear, interconnected view of the entire value chain. Our trusted team of 2,700 experts across 30 countries breaks siloes and connects industries, markets and regions across the globe.


This empowers our customers to identify risk sooner, spot opportunities faster and recalibrate strategy with confidence – whether planning days, weeks, months or decades ahead.


Wood Mackenzie
Intelligence Connected



Wood Mackenzie Brand Video

Wood Mackenzie Values

  • Inclusive – we succeed together
  • Trusting – we choose to trust each other
  • Customer committed – we put customers at the heart of our decisions
  • Future Focused – we accelerate change
  • Curious – we turn knowledge into action

Role Purpose

With ambitious growth goals over the next four to five years, WoodMac Supply Chain Consulting is an exciting place to build a career. With a very strong pipeline over the foreseeable future, our intent is to build out our team with folks capable supporting and driving execution of our upcoming client engagements while helping make our revenue goals achievable. These people will bring strong analytical and communication skills to the table and will have ambition to lead projects and manage client relationships in the future.

In your role as Consultant, you will be responsible for execution and delivery on the projects that you are staffed. You will deliver innovative thinking supported by market research and the subject matter expertise of the collective WoodMac Supply Chain team. You will leverage our software tools to help our energy clients make effective supply chain and capital project execution decisions. You will work closely with your project lead to successfully deliver to the project schedule. You will welcome the opportunity to onboard Consultants who subsequently join the team. We are looking for candidates who are anxious to roll up their sleeves to help us get the work done while enabling the energy transition. You will have opportunities to develop relationships with clients and establish yourself as a trusted advisor.

Main Responsibilities (Serving our Clients)

  • Provide deep analysis of quantitative and qualitative data and synthesize results into meaningful conclusions to help our clients make strategic procurement and capital project decisions
  • Perform market research to assess supply and demand factors influencing our clients' strategic business decisions
  • Support the bidding processes for large capital project contracts and strategic supply chain initiatives, including performing pricing analysis, coordinating bidder correspondence, designing, and orchestrating bidder negotiations and implementing contracts
  • Use WoodMac Energy Intelligence Platform software tools to analyze spend, build custom cost models, forecast escalation, manage eSourcing bid events and support many of our other consulting solutions. This often requires training our clients to harness the value of the WoodMac tools
  • Coordinate / communicate with client supply chain stakeholders as they design and implement supply chain strategies

About You

  • Effective communication and interpersonal skills
  • Highly inquisitive, innovative, organized and detail-oriented

  • Results driven; enjoys the challenge of a changing business environment
  • Willingness to travel 60- 80% of the time

Expectations

  • Personal Impact – a strong sense of self-awareness; understand how others perceive and are impacted by your actions for which you take ownership and accountability
  • Growth Mindset – believe that new abilities can be developed through practice, embrace feedback, motivate others, solve problems and persist
  • Customer Collaboration – the desire to understand who our customers are, to engage effectively, build impactful relationships, and to serve all while keeping them at the heart of our decision making
  • Planning and Prioritizing – a proven ability to plan, prioritize, monitor and manage your own workflows
  • ​​​​​​​Continuous Improvement – an ongoing effort to improve ourselves, our offerings and the way we work​​​​​​​

Other

The General Production Labor position provides hands-on support to production operations by performing a variety of manual and production-related tasks as assigned. This role supports product flow, quality, and efficiency while maintaining a safe work environment and adhering to Tyson policies, food safety standards, and procedures in a fresh food manufacturing environment.

Utility Laborer

Job Description Summary

The Utility Laborer is responsible for maintaining continuous product flow and supporting production operations in a fresh food manufacturing environment. This position relieves Team Members for breaks, fills in during labor shortages, and performs a variety of production support tasks while maintaining a safe work environment and adhering to all Tyson policies, food safety standards, and procedures.

Key Responsibilities

  • Maintain continuous product flow on production lines to support efficiency and throughput

  • Relieve Team Members on the production line for breaks, lunches, and absences

  • Fill in for open positions during labor shortages to ensure uninterrupted operations

  • Perform multiple production tasks as assigned, including but not limited to packing, sorting, staging, and material handling

  • Assist with product movement between production areas to prevent downtime or congestion

  • Monitor work areas to ensure product quality, food safety, and sanitation standards are met

  • Follow all standard operating procedures (SOPs) related to fresh product handling

  • Assist supervisors by responding quickly to changing production needs

  • Identify and report safety hazards, equipment issues, or product concerns immediately

  • Maintain cleanliness and organization of production areas, tools, and equipment

  • Comply with all Tyson policies, OSHA regulations, USDA requirements, and food safety guidelines

  • Perform other duties as assigned to support production and operational goals

Fresh Plant Environment Expectations

  • Work directly with raw and fresh products in a temperature-controlled environment

  • Strict adherence to hygiene, sanitation, and personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements

  • Compliance with food safety, quality, and contamination prevention practices

  • Ability to adapt quickly to changing line assignments and production priorities

Physical Demands and Work Requirements

  • Ability to stand and walk for the entire shift

  • Ability to bend, stoop, reach, twist, and perform repetitive motions

  • Ability to lift, carry, push, and pull materials as required

  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds with or without assistance

  • Ability to work in cold, wet, or humid conditions typical of a fresh plant environment

  • Required use of PPE, including gloves, aprons, hairnets, and protective footwear

Work Schedule

  • Must be available to work assigned shifts

  • Overtime, weekends, and holidays may be required based on production needs

Safety and Compliance Commitment

The Utility Laborer is expected to maintain a safe work environment at all times and strictly adhere to Tyson policies, food safety requirements, OSHA regulations, and plant procedures. This role is critical to ensuring consistent production flow and operational flexibility in a fresh food manufacturing environment.

Relocation Assistance Eligible:

No

Work Shift:

title: GAL Supervisor
description:
Agency

Administrative Office of the Courts

Division

Guardian ad Litem (GAL)
