title: Associate Human Resource Director
description:
What We Can Achieve Together:

As a key member of the Western United States and Canada (WUSCAN) HR team, the Associate Human Resource Director (AHRD) builds strategic partnerships with leaders and HR team members and collaborates across multiple Business Units to implement human-centered and impactful HR initiatives that support The Nature Conservancy’s mission, values and organizational goals. This role is instrumental in fostering an inclusive, high-performing, and equitable culture across the WUSCAN Division. The AHRD leads service delivery and strategic direction in the following human resource functions: employee relations, compensation, talent management, benefits, payroll, staff development and training, organizational development, performance management and recruiting for Canada and the United States. Reporting to the HR Director, the AHRD will manage a team of HR professionals located in multiple locations.

We’re Looking for You:

Are you looking for work you can believe in? At TNC we strive to embody a philosophy of Work that You Can Believe in where you can feel like you are making a difference every day. We’re looking for someone with strong experience in leading a geographically dispersed HR team. The ideal candidate develops business partnerships with senior leaders to establish and implement strategic HR direction to meet TNC's organizational goals and conservation mission. The AHRD works closely with all HR functions to integrate services and deliver timely support to business units. The AHRD also plays a leadership role implementing People strategies in support of ongoing operational improvements and to foster an open, inclusive, transparent, and equitable organizational culture. They will partner with other members of the WUSCAN HR team and People Team to collaboratively share responsibility for designing, developing and implementing innovative People practices aligned with TNC values, strategies and goals. They are experts in Canadian employment law and HR practices and are accountable for delivering relevant support and counsel for the full employee lifecycle in assigned Business Units that are geographically dispersed across Canada and the Western United States. They implement these People Team initiatives to ensure consistency in support of a global, decentralized and geographically dispersed enterprise. This role will supervise a small team of HR professionals supporting WUSCAN and leading the optimization of a new HR operating model in service of the business units. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to the ongoing mission of conservation by directing and shaping the work of our divisional HR team!

We currently have one vacancy for an Associate HR Director.

Responsibilities & Scope:

  • Strategic HR Partnership and Consultation

    • Serve as a primary liaison between the People Team and Business Unit leaders to align HR priorities with business objectives and deliver consistent, high-quality HR practices.

    • Provide strategic counsel on organizational design, workforce planning, operational efficiencies, job creation or elimination, and resource optimization.

    • Advise managers on TNC policy and SOPs, HR processes, employment law and policy requirements, employee engagement, and effective management practices.

  • Employee Relations and Performance Management

    • Promote positive employee relations by facilitating conflict resolution, conducting investigations, and recommending remedies aligned with Conservancy policies, SOPs, competencies, and values.

    • Coach managers and staff on goal setting, timely feedback, continuous development, and high-performance practices.

    • Advise on complex performance management, employee relations, and separations, including voluntary and involuntary terminations, in partnership with HR Legal and senior HR staff as appropriate.

  • Compensation, Equity, and Talent Practices

    • Support job design, job description development, salary guidance, recruitment and offer terms development.

    • Lead team in conducting the annual pay equity analysis and supporting equitable promotion, compensation, and talent decisions.

    • Develop and implement HR programs and strategic initiatives, including talent reviews, succession planning, performance processes and recognition practices.

  • Learning, Development, and HR Service Delivery

    • Assess learning needs, deliver or coordinate HR-related training, build hiring manager capability, and support HR team members and liaisons in managing administrative HR functions.

    • Develop and implement HR standards and client service practices that strengthen consistency, accountability, and support across Business Units.

    • Lead or participate in cross-functional project teams to advance organizational priorities.

  • Team Leadership

    • Supervise a small HR team dedicated to providing exceptional service and support to geographically dispersed business units in Canada and the Western United States.

    • Provide coaching and development opportunities to grow team’s HR expertise and consistency of delivery.

    • Contribute to a culture of psychological safety, innovation, and results orientation.

What You’ll Bring:

  • Bachelor’s degree and 8 years HR related experience supporting 300+ employee client groups in a global, matrixed, complex environment, or equivalent combination.

  • Experience developing and leading multiple HR-related projects and implementing strategic HR programs.

  • Experience supporting employees in both Canada and the United States with demonstrated knowledge of Federal and Provincial employment law including FLSA, ESA, and other related standards.

  • Experience managing the administration, progress, and maintenance of human resource functions in both Canada and the United States, for one or more of the following: employee relations, compensation and performance management, benefits, payroll, staff development/training, organizational development, and recruiting.

  • Experience working with senior managers to root cause HR issues and design, develop and implement HR strategies and initiatives.

  • Experience managing complex employee relations, facilitating and leading crucial conversations, and building effective consultative relationships.

  • Experience supervising HR teams of 2 or more employees, setting work priorities, establishing employee objectives/expectations and driving accountability across the team’s portfolio of work.

  • Experience managing confidential employee matters and employee data in adherence to local laws and data privacy best practices.

  • Experience using MS Office software with experience in constructing and producing reports, data manipulation, and analysis.

  • Ability to travel within the U.S. and Canada up to 10% of time.

  • Ability to work non-standard business hours as needed to accommodate clients in different time zones.

Desired Qualifications:

  • Multi-lingual skills and multi-cultural or cross-cultural experience appreciated.

  • Experience with complex employee mediation.

  • Advanced understanding of HR concepts, processes, and services.

  • Experience developing and implementing HR policies, guidelines and procedures.

  • Experience successfully partnering with and influencing all levels of employees through effective communication skills, written and verbal, and high degree of emotional intelligence.

  • Ability to develop a working knowledge of relevant conservation issues.

  • Experience leading a team and effectively delivering HR services with multiple competing and time-sensitive priorities.

  • Experience developing and delivering presentations and training.

  • Advanced organizational skills and attention to detail.

  • Proven ability to work in a fast paced and highly visible environment.

Salary Information:

Canada

This position may only be based in a Canadian province/territory where TNC is registered (Ontario, Alberta, Northwest Territories). The starting pay range for a candidate selected for this position is generally within the range of $165,000– $170,000 CAD for annual base salary. This range only applies to candidates whose country of employment is Canada. Where a successful candidate’s actual pay will fall within this range will be based on a variety of factors, including, for example, the candidate’s location, qualifications, specific skills, and experience. Your geographic location will be confirmed during the recruitment.

Who We Are:


The Nature Conservancy’s mission is to protect the lands and waters upon which all life depends. As a science-based organization, we create innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that we can create a world in which people and nature thrive. We’re rooted in our mission and guided by our values, which include respect for all people, communities, and cultures. Whether it’s career development, flexible schedules, or a rewarding mission, there’s many reasons to love life inside TNC. Want a better insight to TNC? Check out our TNC Talent playlist on YouTube to hear stories from staff or visit Glassdoor.

One goal is to cultivate an inclusive work environment so that all our colleagues around the globe feel a sense of belonging and that their unique contributions to our mission are valued. In addition to the requirements in our job postings, we recognize that people come with talent and experiences outside of a job and consider each applicant’s unique experience. Please apply – we’d love to hear from you. To quote a popular saying at TNC, “you’ll join for the mission, and stay for the people.”

What We Bring:


Since 1951, TNC has been doing work you can believe in. Through grassroots action, we have grown from a small non-profit into one of the most effective and wide-reaching environmental organizations in the world. Thanks to more than 1 million members, over 400 scientists, and the dedicated efforts of our diverse staff and partners, we impact conservation around the world!

TNC offers competitive and comprehensive benefits packages tailored to the individual countries where we work. These may include health care benefits, retirement benefits, parental leave, paid time off, life insurance, and disability coverage as well as an employee assistance program and other life and well-being benefits. Learn more about our Benefits and Perks here.

We’re proud to offer a flexible work environment that supports the health and well-being of the people we employ.

Our recruiting process includes a rolling interview process to ensure we engage applicants in a timely manner. This means we may review applications in the order in which they are received. Once a strong candidate pool is identified, the role will be unposted. The timeline may vary depending on the expressed interest in the role, so we highly encourage candidates to apply as soon as possible.

Employees must submit their application by logging into Workday and applying via the Jobs Hub.

The Nature Conservancy is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Our commitment to equal employment opportunity includes the recognition that our conservation mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people of all backgrounds, beliefs, and culture. Recruiting and mentoring staff to create an inclusive organization is a priority, and we encourage applicants from all cultures, races, colors, religions, sexes, national or regional origins, ages, disability status, sexual orientation, gender identity, military, protected veteran status or other status protected by law.

The successful applicant must meet the requirements of The Nature Conservancy's background screening process.

TNC is committed to offering accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application process. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please send a note to applyhelp@tnc.org with Request for Accommodation in the subject line.

  • Bachelor’s degree

  • SQL/SAS Coding knowledge and/or experience

title: Conflicts Data Analyst
description:
We are always seeking talented, motivated, growth-minded, and creative individuals. Our firm is committed to providing employee support and advancement, while embracing inclusion and innovation as keys to a stronger future.

We invite you to explore the position below and to submit your application to join our team!

The Conflicts Data Analyst plays a critical role within the Intake & Conflict Services department, supporting the firm's risk management and conflicts clearance processes. The Conflicts Data Analyst is responsible for maintaining the accuracy and integrity of conflicts-related data, with a primary focus on corporate tree structures and entity relationships within the firm's conflicts and financial databases. The Conflicts Data Analyst will review the existing database for accuracy of information and monitor corporate activity and market developments to ensure internal data remains current and reliable.

Essential Responsibilities:

  • Maintain and update conflicts database records, with a focus on corporate tree information including parent-subsidiary and affiliated entity relationships.

  • Research and link parent and child company clients within the conflicts database to ensure accurate entity mapping.

  • Regularly monitor mergers, acquisitions, and other corporate transactions through multiple news sources and research tools, assessing their impact on existing conflicts data.

  • Update database records promptly and accurately in response to corporate structure changes identified through M&A monitoring.

  • Collaborate with ICS team members to resolve data discrepancies.

  • Work cross-functionally with data stakeholders in other administrative departments, primarily Finance and Firm Intelligence, to ensure consistency and alignment of firm data across systems.

  • Assist with quality control reviews of conflicts data to identify and correct gaps or inconsistencies.

  • Support broader ICS operations as needed.

Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Strong attention to detail with the ability to manage and organize large volumes of data accurately.

  • Ability to work independently and prioritize tasks in a fast-paced environment.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

  • Ability to work independently and collaborate effectively with ICS team members and administrative departments.

  • Strong commitment to client service, ethical conduct, and firm values.

  • Ability to work effectively and efficiently in remote, hybrid, and in-office environments.

Required Education:

Preferred Education:

  • N/A

Required Qualifications:

  • Minimum three (3) years of experience in corporate research, identifying affiliate relationships, data monitoring, and/or database maintenance.

  • Strong proficiency in research tools and online databases.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in a law firm, legal research, or library environment.

  • Prior experience in a conflicts or risk management role beneficial.

  • Familiarity with Dunn & Bradstreet as well as concepts of corporate affiliates and Global Ultimate Owners beneficial.

description:
At Sunrun, we’re on a mission to change the way the world interacts with energy, and we’re building a company and brand that puts power at the center of life. To do it, we’re designing a dynamic culture where employee development, well-being, and safety come first. It’s why we’ve become the #1 home solar and battery company in America. We’re unlike any other residential energy company. Our vertically integrated model gives us total control over every part of the energy lifecycle – from sale through installation and beyond – so you can find endless opportunities for growth. Come join a career you can grow in and a culture you can run with.

We’re on a mission to make energy more reliable and affordable for more people. We provide an opportunity with storage and solar to help people access greater energy independence without the big upfront costs. Sunrun is the largest dedicated residential solar and storage company in the country and has a mission to bring stably priced resilient power to the masses.

Since 2007, Sunrun has grown into America's #1 home solar and battery company. We got here by putting our people’s safety and growth first. That’s why we created the Power+ program: to invest in your skills. We train you to work across different teams—from qualifying homes for solar, to installing, to inspecting the final work, and servicing existing systems. This versatility helps limit reduced hours and enhances job security in an industry affected by seasons. It also means you can solve customer problems in one visit, keeping you safely off the road and moving your career forward.

The Foreman position provides leadership and technical expertise for a solar installation crew of three to six members. The Foreman is responsible for safety, quality, customer service, and productivity and ensures the successful completion of residential and small commercial projects.

  • Computer skills with Microsoft Excel and Word

  • Excellent communication, interpersonal and people management skills

  • Ability to work with chemicals using appropriate protections

title: NPI Product Manager (Woodbridge, ON)
description:
When joining PerkinElmer, you select an experienced and trusted leader in scientific solutions, with the support of a global service network and distribution centers, providing the right solution, at the right time, to meet critical customer needs. With over an 80+ year legacy of advancing science and a mission of innovating for a healthier world, our dedicated team collaborates closely with commercial, government, academic and healthcare customers to deliver our broad portfolio of analytical solutions, and OneSource services.

Job Title

NPI Product Manager (Woodbridge, ON)


Location(s)

Woodbridge

Job Description

PerkinElmer is seeking an NPI Product Manager to serve as the dedicated commercial lead for a single major New Product Introduction programme. This is a purpose-built role with one clear mandate: ensure that a new analytical instrument arrives in market fully commercially ready — with the pricing, positioning, training, launch plan, and commercial tools that allow it to ramp revenue quickly and establish a durable market position.

The NPI PM owns commercial readiness from development programme initiation through post-launch ramp. They work in close partnership with R&D, Applications Science, Marketing, and the field commercial organisation — but they are not embedded in R&D. Their job is to represent the market and the customer in every programme decision: challenging technical choices that create commercial risk, driving VOC to sharpen positioning, and ensuring the launch plan reflects what is actually needed to win — not just what is convenient to deliver.

This role requires deep programme discipline, commercial instinct, and the interpersonal credibility to lead cross-functional teams without formal authority. The NPI PM must be comfortable operating in ambiguity, making evidence-based decisions under time pressure, and holding a high bar for commercial readiness even when programme timelines create pressure to compromise.

Responsibilities:

Commercial Readiness Ownership

  • Own the commercial readiness workstream for the assigned NPI programme — defining what 'launch-ready' means commercially and driving the organisation to achieve it
  • Develop and maintain the NPI commercial launch plan: pricing strategy, target customer profiles, positioning framework, competitive differentiation, channel and regional launch sequencing, and sales readiness milestones
  • Set and own launch pricing — building the pricing model from market research, customer willingness-to-pay data, competitive benchmarking, and lifecycle revenue objectives; seeking approval through the VP Product Line
  • Define and track commercial readiness gate criteria for each NPI stage gate — ensuring commercial preparation keeps pace with technical development and that the launch team never arrives at gate approval without a complete commercial plan

Market Requirements & Product Definition

  • Own the Market Requirements Document (MRD) for the assigned NPI — working with the Strategic Segment Manager and conducting independent VOC to ensure requirements are grounded in customer evidence, not internal assumption
  • Translate MRD requirements into a clear Product Requirements Document (PRD) that R&D can act on — making explicit priority trade-offs between must-have and nice-to-have requirements
  • Serve as the primary commercial interface to the R&D programme team — attending technical reviews, raising commercial risk flags early, and negotiating feature/schedule trade-offs with the VP Product Line's backing
  • Monitor competitive landscape throughout the programme — tracking competitive instrument releases, pricing moves, and application developments that affect the NPI's positioning assumptions

Voice of Customer & Validation

  • Design and lead the NPI VOC programme — a minimum of 30 in-depth customer interviews per year during active development, structured around requirements validation, concept testing, and pricing research
  • Manage beta customer relationships from site selection through beta completion — ensuring beta programmes generate evidence-based feedback, not goodwill gestures
  • Translate VOC findings into actionable programme recommendations: feature priority changes, pricing adjustments, positioning refinements, or competitive response requirements

Launch Execution & Field Readiness

  • Own the commercial launch plan — coordinating across Applications Science, MarComm, Regional Marketing, Sales, and Service to ensure every function is launch-ready on day one
  • Develop the commercial launch toolkit: product brief, competitive battlecard, value proposition messaging, demo guide, and objection-handling resource for the field commercial team
  • Deliver product and application training to the sales and service organisation pre-launch — ensuring commercial teams can demonstrate, position, and close against competitive alternatives
  • Monitor post-launch commercial KPIs during the ramp period — order intake, revenue, competitive win rate, and pricing realisation — and lead corrective action where ramp performance lags plan

Programme Collaboration

  • Attend and actively contribute to NPI programme reviews, stage-gate meetings, and executive steering committee briefings — representing the commercial perspective at every programme milestone
  • Partner with the Applications Scientist to develop the application note and proof-of-performance content roadmap that supports the NPI launch and early ramp
  • Handoff the NPI to the Strategic PM and Operations PM at commercial launch — providing full product, pricing, and market documentation, and supporting a clean transition of ongoing portfolio management responsibility

Success Metrics

  • Commercial launch plan completeness at each stage gate (vs. defined readiness criteria)
  • Post-launch revenue ramp vs. AOP plan — 3-month, 6-month, and 12-month actuals
  • VOC programme coverage — minimum 30 documented customer conversations per active programme year
  • Pricing realisation — average selling price vs. list price in the launch period
  • Sales organisation launch readiness score (training completion, demo capability certification)
  • Competitive win rate in the first 12 months post-launch

Qualifications & Experience:

Required

  • 8+ years of experience in product management, technical product marketing, or programme management within analytical instrumentation, life sciences tools, or scientific capital equipment
  • Demonstrated experience leading a major NPI through full commercial launch — from market requirements definition through post-launch ramp, with clear personal ownership of commercial readiness deliverables
  • Deep working knowledge of at least one analytical technique relevant to PerkinElmer's portfolio (spectroscopy, chromatography, mass spectrometry, materials characterisation) — sufficient to engage credibly with R&D teams and customers in technical programme discussions
  • Experience conducting structured VOC programmes — customer interviewing, concept testing, willingness-to-pay research — and translating findings into product and positioning decisions
  • Strong financial acumen: experience building NPI business cases, pricing models, and revenue ramp forecasts
  • Proven ability to lead cross-functional programme teams without direct authority — influencing R&D, Applications, MarComm, and regional commercial functions through credibility and programme structure
  • Ability to travel 25–35% for customer visits, beta site management, conferences, and internal programme reviews

Preferred

  • MSc or PhD in a relevant scientific discipline — providing peer-level credibility with R&D teams and scientifically trained customers
  • Experience in a structured stage-gate NPI process within a product management organisation
  • Familiarity with PerkinElmer's specific instrument categories and customer workflows
  • Track record of competitive win in a head-to-head NPI situation — launching a product that displaced an established competitive platform

The annual compensation range for this full-time position is $120,000.00 to $131,000.00. The final base pay offered to the successful candidate will be determined by factors including internal equity, work location, as well as individual qualifications, such as job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

Working at ALS

The ALS team is a diverse and dedicated community united by our passion to make a difference in the world.

Our values are important to us, and shape how we work, how we treat each other and how we recognise excellence.

At ALS, you’ll be supported to develop new skills and reach your full potential. We invest in our people with programs and opportunities that help you build a diverse career with us.

Please apply on-line and provide a resume & cover letter that best demonstrate your motivation and ability to meet the requirements of this role.

title: Data analyst - Business Lending
description:
Data Analyst - Business Lending

Do you have a talent for taking it on and making it happen, enthusiasm for helping others to be successful and a knack for always being a step ahead? Do you strive to bring fresh ideas to life and embrace challenges in a fast changing and complex environment? Are you a naturally collaborative person who listens and invests in others to achieve common goals, who challenges the status quo and is eager to propose creative solutions to problems? Then you are the perfect new colleague we are looking for!

Roles and responsibilities

As a Data Analyst within Tribe Business Lending you will:

  • Play a key role in supporting the data‑driven culture behind the digitalization of loan origination, in‑life management, and risk monitoring across our customer journeys.

  • Analyse lending processes of our customers and deliver insights as well as bring structural solutions to business problems of product teams and leadership to support data driven decision making in digital transformation.

  • Play an end to end role in analysing the business problem, identifying data requirements, involving in getting the data into datalake, building queries and delivering ad-hoc or structural reports.

  • Align with stakeholders across products (CJE and Developers), Data Management and Data Engineers to define and execute end to end implementation plans

  • Build and maintain Power BI dashboards to enable real-time portfolio insights

  • Deliver consistent, explainable, and auditable reporting and insights for internal and external stakeholders, including portfolio performance, operational steering, and data quality monitoring.

  • Act as a data steward, including capturing new data into the data lake and safeguarding data definitions.

The team

As a Data Analyst, you will be part of the Tribe Business Lending Netherlands. You support our purpose: “Focus on easy, smart and personal end-to-end business lending journeys”. We empower entrepreneurs to stay a step ahead with easy, smart and personal business lending services. You will be working in an Agile environment by being a member of a multidisciplinary team of 8 to 9 specialists. Your colleagues will have a background in Process management, IT, Data Analytics/Management in the business domain. You work closely with the colleagues from Products, Pricing, Operations, Credit Risk and Finance.

How to succeed

We are looking for a colleague with a talent for taking it on and making it happen, enthusiasm for helping others to be successful and a knack for always being a step ahead. In other words, you strive to bring fresh ideas to life and embrace challenges in a fast changing and complex environment. You are a naturally collaborative person who listens and invests in others to achieve common goals. You love to challenge the status quo and are eager to propose creative solutions to problems. We hire smart people like you for your potential. Our biggest expectation is that you’ll stay curious. Keep learning. Take on responsibility. In return, we’ll back you to develop into an even more awesome version of yourself.

  • Master’s degree in mathematics, Econometrics, Computer Science, Information Management, AI, Statistics or alike, and/ or equivalent experience within data reporting & statistics.

  • 3+ years experience as data analyst

  • You are analytically strong and are a star in assessing and solving problems, making analyses, and sharing results with impact

  • You are an expert with query languages (e.g., SQL, SAS) and dashboarding tooling (e.g. Cognos Analytics, Power BI)

  • Affinity or experience with Business Lending and Business Banking

  • To be able to influence and convince not only peers but also the stakeholders based on analytical results.

  • Communicatively strong, team player and someone who takes initiative and ownership

  • You are fluent in English (verbal and written) and hold current residency in the Netherlands.

Rewards and benefits
We want to make sure that it’s possible for you to strike the right balance between your career and your private life. Find out more about our employment conditions.


The benefits of working with us at ING include:

  • A salary tailored to your qualities and experience (scale 9 to 10) based on a 36 or 40 hour working week

  • 25-28 vacation days depending on contract

  • Pension scheme

  • Benefits budget consisting of individual savings contribution (BIS), 13th month salary and holiday allowance.

  • Hybrid way of working to blend working from home for focus and working from office (Amsterdam) for collaboration and co-creation

  • Personal growth and challenging work with endless possibilities

  • An informal working environment with innovative colleagues

description:

Specific Responsibilities

  • Conduct testing using rougher flotation, gravity separation, or cyanide leaching techniques;

description:

Job Description:

About the Job:

This is a hands-on, execution-heavy role within Sun Life's startup-style innovation team focused on rapidly designing, building, and scaling transformative digital products- including an agentic AI platform and new client experience solutions. Reporting to the Director of Engineering, In-House Accelerator, you will own the full product lifecycle from concept to launch, writing production code, making pragmatic architecture decisions, and shipping working software quickly in a regulated environment. This role demands both technical excellence and entrepreneurial ownership, combining the agility of a startup with the resources and impact of a global enterprise. You will build products from zero, deliver them to users, and own the outcomes of your work.


What You’ll Do?

Own products end‑to‑end

  • Use AI-assisted development and coding agents to accelerate prototyping, implementation, testing, debugging, and code review without compromising engineering quality.

  • Make pragmatic technical decisions that balance speed, quality, scalability, and business impact.

  • Own outcomes. If something isn’t working, you fix it.

Build fast, learn faster

  • Prototype quickly, launch MVPs, run experiments, and validate ideas with real users.

  • Instrument everything, gather feedback, and iterate based on data.

Lead by building

  • Write production‑quality code daily while guiding the technical direction of the team.

  • Establish lightweight architecture and engineering practices that enable speed without chaos.

  • Provide clear technical leadership through code reviews, design discussions, and mentorship.

Collaborate across disciplines

  • Work directly with product managers, designers, and business stakeholders to turn ambiguous problems into working software.

  • Clearly communicate trade‑offs, risks, and timelines to both technical and non‑technical audiences.

Shape the future

  • Champion modern engineering practices, tools, and technologies that give us a competitive edge.

  • Build reusable components and technical foundations that accelerate future products.

What You Bring?

Engineering depth & versatility

  • 7–10 years of hands-on engineering experience, with recent, demonstrable coding work.

  • Demonstrated experience using AI-assisted development tools as part of day-to-day software development, with strong practices for prompting, code review, testing, security, and validating AI-generated code.

  • Experience designing and building microservices, APIs, and distributed systems that scale.

Product mindset

  • You think in terms of user value, not just technical elegance.

  • You’re comfortable making decisions with incomplete information and adjusting as you learn.

  • You bias toward action, experimentation, and learning over perfection.

Cloud & delivery fluency

  • Hands‑on experience deploying and operating software in the cloud (AWS, Azure).

  • Comfortable with CI/CD, containers, and shipping code to production frequently.

  • A solid handle on performance, observability, security, and resilient system design.

Leadership & communication

  • Proven ability to influence technical direction without relying on hierarchy.

  • Experience mentoring engineers and raising the bar through example.

  • Strong communication skills. You can explain complex systems simply and persuasively.

Nice to Have:

  • Experience in startups, accelerators, or innovation labs.

  • Experience with AI/ML systems → building with LLMs, prompt engineering, or agentic architectures.


Why This Role?

  • High-Impact Work: Build products that directly shape Sun Life's future, with your code reaching real users quickly.

  • Leadership Opportunity: Lead technical direction, mentor others, and shape the engineering culture of a growing team.

  • Autonomy and Ownership: Make decisions, drive solutions, and see the direct impact of your work.

  • Learn and Grow Fast: Exposure to new technologies, business problems, and the full product lifecycle in a compressed timeframe.

  • Collaborative, Innovative Culture: Work with passionate, talented people who move fast and support each other.

  • Flexible Workstyle: Hybrid or office-based as required by the role.

What’s in it for you?

  • Being a member of the Sun Life family, a group of people united by our Purpose: to help Clients and Employees achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives.

  • An environment of continuous learning, development, and improvement.

  • Internal mobility is supported by leaders who are dedicated to fueling your professional growth.


The Base Pay range is for the primary location for which the job is posted. It may vary depending on the work location of the successful candidate or other factors. In addition to Base Pay, eligible Sun Life employees participate in various incentive plans, payment under which is discretionary and subject to individual and company performance. Certain sales focused roles have sales incentive plans based on individual or group sales results.


Diversity and inclusion have always been at the core of our values at Sun Life. A diverse workforce with wide perspectives and creative ideas benefits our Clients, the communities where we operate and all of us as colleagues. We welcome applications from qualified individuals from all backgrounds.


Persons with disabilities who need accommodation in the application process, or those needing job postings in an alternative format, may e-mail a request to thebrightside@sunlife.com.

title: CRM Program Manager
description:
If you're ready to be part of our legacy of hope and innovation, we encourage you to take the first step and explore our current job openings. Your best is waiting to be discovered.

Day - 08 Hour (United States of America)

This is a Stanford Health Care job.

A Brief Overview
Stanford Health Care's Enterprise Contact Center (ECC) serves as a shared services platform supporting patient scheduling, nurse triage, referral coordination, and multi-specialty contact center operations across the SHC care delivery network. The CRM Program Manager owns the Epic CRM program for the enterprise contact center ecosystem — the taxonomy, standards, governance, and operational workflows that determine how every patient contact is categorized, routed, documented, and reported. This role is the connective tissue between Epic's Contact Hub and CRM capabilities, the Panviva knowledge base, the new omnichannel platform's CTI integration, and the operational teams who rely on all of them working together seamlessly. Business requirements, workflow validation, UAT, and operational sign-off are owned by this role; Epic/TDS teams own technical build, configuration, functional testing, and integration testing.

Locations
Stanford Health Care

What you will do
  • Epic CRM Program Ownership
  • Owns the Epic CRM program including taxonomy, standards, foundational structure, and governance to ensure consistency across ECC and non-ECC contact center teams.
  • Defines the CRM standards framework for new builds, modifications, naming conventions, categories, outcomes, and documentation practices, and hold Epic/TDS technical teams accountable for consistent application across all contact center environments to support operational consistency, reporting integrity, and omnichannel readiness.
  • Serves as the single business owner of the CRM data model — defining and enforcing the hierarchy of contact types, categories, subcategories, dispositions, and follow-up actions that agents select to classify every patient interaction across the enterprise, ensuring the taxonomy supports cascading navigation and consistent disposition selection.
  • Epic Contact Hub & Workflow Operations
  • Serves as the operational lead for Epic Contact Hub workflows, ensuring configurations, CRM workflows, and the agent experience remain aligned to operational needs and future omnichannel capabilities.
  • Develops deep expertise in Epic scheduling decision trees and own the navigation between CRM workflows and decision tree usage to create a seamless staff experience and reduce workflow friction during patient interactions.
  • Designs and optimizes agent-facing workflows that minimize clicks, reduce cognitive load, and guide staff through complex patient scenarios (multi-department scheduling, referral chains, prior authorization) with contextual CRM prompts.
  • Leads User Acceptance Testing (UAT) for CRM workflow changes prior to deployment, validating that business requirements are met and operational workflows perform as expected; functional testing, configuration testing, and integration testing are owned by Epic/TDS technical teams.
  • Knowledge Base Alignment & Content Governance
  • Ensures CRM follow-up actions, dispositions, and next steps are appropriately classified and aligned with Panviva knowledge base content so that guidance remains intuitive, duplication is minimized, and staff receive a consistent experience across systems.
  • Partners with the knowledge management team to maintain a mapping between CRM disposition codes and corresponding Panviva articles — ensuring that when an agent selects a disposition, the relevant guidance surfaces automatically.
  • Identifies and remediates content drift: cases where CRM workflow changes have made knowledge base articles stale, or where new knowledge base content requires corresponding CRM taxonomy updates.
  • Supports the transition from Panviva to any future knowledge management platform (e.g., CXone Expert, Genesys Knowledge) by ensuring CRM-to-KB mappings are documented and portable.
  • Governance, Intake & Change Management
  • Oversees CRM governance, intake, prioritization, and change review to ensure CRM changes are vetted against standards and evaluated for impact to routing logic, reporting, Contact Hub workflows, knowledge base dependencies, and integrations.
  • Partners with Epic, TDS, operations, PMO, and other stakeholders to evaluate CRM-related requests, define business requirements, and assess downstream impact prior to implementation.
  • Establishes a CRM change advisory process: no CRM taxonomy or workflow change goes to production without documented impact assessment covering routing, reporting, KB alignment, and agent experience.
  • Owns the end-to-end operational change management for omnichannel CTI and Epic CRM rollout, ensuring workflows, documentation standards, staff readiness, and adoption are implemented in a coordinated manner.
  • Develops and delivers CRM-specific training for new agents, supervisors, and operational leads — not just how to use the system, but why the taxonomy matters and how their inputs drive downstream reporting and patient experience.
  • Reporting & Data Integrity
  • Drives CRM reporting maturity by partnering on reporting standards, data integrity, and sustainable reporting structures to support operational insights and decision-making.
  • Defines and monitors CRM data quality metrics: disposition completion rates, categorization accuracy, decision tree completion rates, and follow-up action closure rates.
  • Partners with the Reporting/BI Analyst to design CRM-sourced dashboards that give operations leaders visibility into contact patterns, resolution rates, escalation trends, and agent workflow efficiency.
  • Identifies and resolves systemic data quality issues — e.g., high volumes of “Other” or “Miscellaneous” dispositions that indicate taxonomy gaps or training deficits.
  • Omnichannel Readiness & Platform Integration
  • Serves as the CRM subject matter expert for the omnichannel platform migration, ensuring that CRM taxonomy, workflows, and decision trees are compatible with the new platform’s CTI integration, screen pop design, and agent desktop.
  • Partners with the Solution Architect and Integration Engineers to define how CRM data flows between Epic and the omnichannel platform — which fields populate the screen pop, which dispositions write back to Epic, and which events trigger CRM workflow updates.
  • Evaluates how new omnichannel capabilities (chat, SMS, email, voicebot) impact the CRM taxonomy — ensuring that digital channel contacts are classified consistently with voice contacts and that reporting integrity is maintained across channels.
  • Contributes to the platform product roadmap by identifying CRM-driven enhancement opportunities: new disposition codes for emerging contact types, decision tree refinements based on contact pattern analysis, and workflow optimizations based on agent feedback.

Education Qualifications
  • Bachelor’s degree in a work-related field from an accredited college or university is required
  • Master’s in Health Informatics, Healthcare Administration, or Information Systems is preferred.

Experience Qualifications
  • 7+ years of experience in healthcare IT, contact center operations, or healthcare business operations, with demonstrated working knowledge of Epic CRM, Contact Hub, or scheduling workflows from a business governance or operations perspective.
  • Preferred experience: o Experience with Master Data Management principles, data normalization, and CRM taxonomy design o Experience with omnichannel contact center platforms (NICE CXone, Genesys Cloud, or equivalent) and their Epic integration models (SpinSci, Health CX, or native CTI). o Experience with Panviva or similar knowledge management platforms in a healthcare contact center environment. o Familiarity with contact center reporting tools and metrics (AHT, FCR, disposition analysis, contact categorization accuracy). o Experience in an academic medical center or multi-entity health system with complex scheduling and referral workflows. o Experience leading Epic CRM build or optimization projects through the full lifecycle: requirements, design, build, test, train, go-live, and post-live optimization.

Required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities
  • Working knowledge of Epic Contact Hub and CRM workflows from a business operations perspective; Epic certification not required. Familiarity with how Epic CRM data structures support routing logic, reporting, and agent navigation is expected.
  • Demonstrated experience building and maintaining CRM taxonomy, governance frameworks, and workflow standards in a multi-site or multi-specialty healthcare environment.
  • Strong understanding of knowledge base management principles and experience integrating KB content (Panviva, KMS, or equivalent) with CRM workflows.
  • Experience with contact center operations: understanding of ACD routing logic, disposition coding, agent workflows, and how CRM data drives operational reporting.
  • Proven ability to manage change in a complex stakeholder environment — partnering with clinical operations, IT, training, and vendor teams to implement workflow changes without disrupting patient-facing operations.
  • Excellent analytical skills: ability to identify data quality issues, trace reporting discrepancies to their root cause in CRM configuration, and design sustainable fixes.
  • Strong documentation and communication skills: ability to write CRM standards, governance procedures, and training materials that non-technical operational staff can follow.

Licenses and Certifications
  • PMP - Project Mgmt Professional preferred . or
  • CAPM - Certified Associate In Project Mgmt preferred .


These principles apply to ALL employees:

SHC Commitment to Providing an Exceptional Patient & Family Experience

Stanford Health Care sets a high standard for delivering value and an exceptional experience for our patients and families. Candidates for employment and existing employees must adopt and execute C-I-CARE standards for all of patients, families and towards each other. C-I-CARE is the foundation of Stanford’s patient-experience and represents a framework for patient-centered interactions. Simply put, we do what it takes to enable and empower patients and families to focus on health, healing and recovery.

You will do this by executing against our three experience pillars, from the patient and family’s perspective:

  • Know Me: Anticipate my needs and status to deliver effective care
  • Show Me the Way: Guide and prompt my actions to arrive at better outcomes and better health
  • Coordinate for Me: Own the complexity of my care through coordination

Accordingly, SHC does not discriminate against any person on the basis of race, color, sex, sexual orientation or gender identity and/or expression, religion, age, national or ethnic origin, political beliefs, marital status, medical condition, genetic information, veteran status, or disability, or the perception of any of the above. People of all genders, members of all racial and ethnic groups, people with disabilities, and veterans are encouraged to apply. Qualified applicants with criminal convictions will be considered after an individualized assessment of the conviction and the job requirements.

title: Delivery Technician - Monroeville, PA
description:
At Accendra Health, we understand that healthcare is complex, and we’re here to make it easier. We help deliver care beyond traditional settings, making essential products and services more accessible through every stage of life. As part of the care team, our teammates play a critical role in delivering personalized, long-term care for the patients we serve.

With deep expertise promoting health outside the hospital and a presence in communities nationwide through our Apria and Byram Healthcare brands, Accendra Health does more than just deliver the essentials.

If you’re interested in meaningful work with impact, explore our career opportunities and join us in our purpose of Bringing Care To Life™.

About the Role

The Delivery Technician delivers, sets up, and picks up durable medical equipment (DME) in patient homes. You will educate patients on basic equipment use and ensure safe operation while providing high-quality customer service.

Why This Delivery Technician Role Is Different

This role plays a critical part in supporting patient safety, comfort, and independence. At our Portsmouth branch, you’ll join a small, supportive, tight-knit team where you’re known, valued, and trusted. You’re not just dropping off equipment; you’re providing essential support to patients in their homes.

Key Highlights

  • Smaller branch with close teamwork and strong support

  • Most techs take their trucks home based on route and schedule

  • Clear on-call expectations with transparent rotation

  • Hands-on role with mechanical and patient-facing responsibilities

  • Stable schedule with flexibility

  • Safe Driver Bonus eligible

Schedule

  • Monday–Friday, 10:00 AM–6:30 PM

On-Call Transparency

  • On-call every 4 weeks

  • Rotation runs Monday–Sunday

  • Paid an on-call stipend

  • Paid from the moment you leave home for a call

  • Overtime paid if on-call causes over 40 hours in the week

  • Most callouts occur Saturday night and Sunday daytime

Travel Requirements

  • Service radius up to 120–160 miles per day

  • Most technicians take their trucks home unless they are unable

Salary Range

  • $19.60–$20.96 per hour

  • Pay varies based on experience, skills, and location

  • Eligible for Safe Driver Bonus

What You’ll Do

  • Safely lift, carry, and maneuver equipment weighing up to 50 lbs. as part of daily deliveries and setups

  • Deliver, set up, and pick up DME and supplies inside patient homes

  • Provide clear, compassionate, professional instruction on equipment use

  • Offer a high level of customer service and support to patients who may rely on this equipment for life-sustaining needs

  • Load and unload equipment from the delivery vehicle

  • Respond to emergency delivery requests when needed

  • Complete delivery logs, pickup forms, and vehicle documentation accurately

  • Maintain supply components in patient profiles

  • Assist with equipment cleaning and minor repairs

  • Perform routine vehicle checks

  • Support additional duties as assigned

Required

  • Ability to lift, carry and maneuver equipment weighing up to 50 lbs. as part of daily deliveries and set-ups

  • High school diploma or equivalent

  • No experience required!

  • 21 years of age or older

  • Valid driver’s license

  • Completion of Apria’s Driver Training Program

  • English reading, writing, and speaking skills

Top Attributes for Success

  • Willingness to learn

  • Dependability

  • Adaptability

  • Strong customer service and bedside manner

  • Mechanical aptitude

  • Comfort entering patient homes

Why You’ll Love Working Here

  • You make a meaningful impact on patients' lives

  • Supportive small-team environment

  • Transparent and hands-on leadership

  • Predictable schedule with some flexibility

  • Training and development opportunities

  • Independent work with strong team support

Teammate Benefits

As an Accendra Health employee, you have choices to fit your life. Our comprehensive benefits program is designed to meet you where you are — through all of life’s stages. We’ve got you and your family covered with benefits that support your health, finances, and overall wellness.

Our benefits program includes:

  • Medical, dental, and vision care coverage

  • Paid time off plan

  • 401(k) Plan

  • Flexible Spending Accounts

  • Basic life insurance

  • Short-and long-term disability coverage

  • Accident insurance

  • Teammate Assistance Program

  • Paid parental leave

  • Domestic partner benefits

  • Mental, physical, and financial well-being programs

If you feel this opportunity could be the next step in your career, we encourage you to apply.

Accendra is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, genetic information, religion, disability, age, status as a veteran, or any other status prohibited by applicable national, federal, state or local law.

All resumes submitted by search firms to any employee at our Company via email, the Internet, or in any form and/or method without a valid written search agreement in place for this position will be deemed the sole property of our Company. No fee will be paid in the event the candidate is hired by our Company as a result of the referral or through other means.

title: Private Banker I
description:

The Private Banker I is responsible for comprehensive management and service delivery, specifically catered to Simmons Private Banking and high-net-worth customers.   • A Bachelor’s degree in business, finance, related field, or relevant job experience is preferred.

  • 2+ years banking experience with basic sales skills and elevated customer service are preferred.

  • Experience in the local market required for better understanding of the environment and potential customer base.

Computer Skills

Certificates, Licenses, Registrations

Other Qualifications (including physical requirements)

title: Revenue Cycle Managed Services - AR Supervisor
description:
Impact Advisors, LLC is a nationally recognized healthcare management consulting firm delivering Best in KLAS advisory, implementation, and optimization services. We are driven by a commitment to exceed client expectations and are proud to be a trusted partner to many of the nation's leading healthcare organizations. Our mission to drive patient-centered, value-driven outcomes has earned us prestigious industry accolades. To learn more about us, visit

Impact Advisors is seeking a dynamic and motivated AR Supervisor. This supervisor will be responsible for managing a group of near shore AR representatives and driving cash collections for a provider system. The AR Supervisor plays a critical frontline leadership role and serves as a partner to AR Managers and Directors, supporting both team performance and client outcomes.

Extensive travel to Mexico City OR ability to expatriate to Mexico for 1 year required.

The AR Supervisor manages between 10-15 AR representatives in a nearshore location. This position will play a key leadership position in the continued growth and optimization of Impact Advisors' nearshore revenue cycle operations. The AR Supervisor will partner with US and Mexico-based leadership teams to support workforce development, operational consistency, and scalable delivery models that drive client outcomes. The position requires regular travel to Mexico, including extended stays of up to three weeks every other month, to support onboarding, training, team engagement, operational oversight, and leadership development activities.

This position reports to the AR Director and offers a unique opportunity to contribute to client success while making a meaningful impact on the healthcare industry.

Key Responsibilities:

Daily Operational Oversight:

  • Monitor key AR performance metrics including cash collections, aged AR, denial rates, productivity, quality scores, accounts worked, and payer-specific trends to ensure achievement of client and organizational targets.
  • Ensure timely escalation and resolution of payer issues, including payment delays, contract discrepancies, authorization concerns, and systemic billing barriers impacting cash flow
  • Conduct account audits and quality reviews to validate follow-up accuracy, documentation standards, appeal effectiveness, and compliance with client and regulatory requirements.
  • Oversee management of high-dollar and high-priority accounts, ensuring appropriate escalation and resolution strategies are implemented to maximize reimbursement.
  • Review escalated or complex claims requiring supervisor intervention, and support resolution for those claims, while incorporating training to the rep.

Staff Leadership:

  • Partner with leadership to develop and execute workforce planning strategies, including onboarding, training, and capacity management for expanding nearshore teams.
  • Lead, coach, and evaluate AR Representatives to meet productivity, quality, and accuracy standards.
  • Partner with a local near shore leader to become an expert in US Healthcare and AR
  • Conduct regular 1:1 meetings, team huddles, and performance discussions.
  • Support disciplinary action or escalation as needed.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Establish and monitor operational performance metrics, identifying opportunities to improve efficiency, quality, employee engagement, and client outcomes within the nearshore delivery model.
  • Work closely with AR Managers, Directors, and Client Delivery leadership to escalate payer issues, recommend process improvements, and support client‑focused outcomes.
  • Foster alignment between US-based and nearshore teams by promoting consistent communication, knowledge sharing, process adoption, and accountability across locations.
  • Participate in leadership or operational meetings as needed.

Required

  • 3+ years of experience in healthcare Accounts Receivable, including follow‑up, denials, and appeals.
  • At least 1–2 years of AR team lead or supervisor experience.
  • Strong understanding of revenue cycle processes, billing workflows, and payer behavior.
  • Proficiency with EHR and billing systems, Microsoft Excel, and workflow reporting tools.
  • Excellent communication, time management, and organizational skills.
  • Ability and willingness to travel to Mexico for extended periods, including approximately three weeks every other month, to support operational leadership, training, onboarding, team development, and business growth initiatives. Opportunity to expatriate for a year is also available.

Preferred

  • Hands‑on AR experience with California payers and billing standards.
  • Experience supporting large, multi‑facility health systems.
  • Bilingual (English/Spanish)
  • Experience in complex denial management environments.
  • Experience supporting and leading teams within a nearshore or offshore delivery model.
  • Experience scaling nearshore operations, including workforce planning, process standardization, and performance management across distributed teams.

For salaried positions, this role may also be eligible for an annual performance bonus. Additional benefits and perks may also be available, depending on the position and employment terms. This range reflects consideration of several factors, including skills, experience, training, certifications, and organizational needs.

Our People and Culture

At Impact Advisors, we cultivate a caring, fun, honest, and autonomous work environment. Our success stems from our associates' dedication and a shared mission to create a “Positive Impact.” We embrace diversity and inclusion, fostering an environment where all employees feel valued and empowered.

Join Impact Advisors and make a real difference in healthcare.

title: Senior Client Program Manager
description:
TELUS Health is empowering every person to live their healthiest life. Guided by our vision, we are leveraging the power of our leading edge technology and focusing on the uniqueness of each individual to create the future of health. As a global-leading health and well-being provider – encompassing physical, mental and financial health – TELUS Health is improving health outcomes for consumers, patients, healthcare professionals, employers and employees.

Join our team and what we'll accomplish together

At TELUS Health, we're not just managing retirement and benefits programs—we're transforming how organizations deliver them. Our Retirement & Benefit Solutions team powers cloud-based platforms that touch millions of lives across North America. Every day, we help our clients modernize systems that matter: pension administration, benefits delivery, health & welfare programs.

As a Senior Client Program Manager, you'll be the orchestrator of some of our most strategic client relationships. You'll lead the delivery of large-scale transformations—whether that's migrating organizations to the cloud, modernizing legacy pension systems, or rolling out enterprise health & welfare platforms. You'll partner directly with executive stakeholders, drive governance that actually works, and translate complex technical work into measurable business outcomes.

This is not a back-office role. You'll be in the room with C-suite clients, shaping how their organizations deliver benefits to their employees. You'll own the delivery narrative, manage the complexity, and ensure that ambitious programs land successfully—on time, on budget, and with lasting client impact.

What you'll do

Own Large-Scale Client Delivery Lead end-to-end delivery of complex Defined Benefit, Defined Contribution, and Health & Welfare programs. That means juggling multiple workstreams, coordinating across Product, Development, Configuration, Data, QA, and Operations. You'll manage dependencies, mitigate risks, forecast financial performance, and keep everyone aligned to what actually matters: delivering on commitments.

Be the Strategic Client Partner You'll be the senior delivery voice for our most important clients. Build trusted relationships with executive stakeholders. Lead steering committees. Have the conversations that shape strategy, not just status. Proactively identify where we can modernize, improve, and create value—thinking like a consultant, not just a delivery manager.

Drive Governance & Decision-Making Establish governance frameworks that don't slow things down—they accelerate them. Set up escalation paths that work. Deliver clear, data-driven executive reporting that helps clients and internal leaders make confident decisions. Make sure program health, risks, and financial impacts are visible and actionable.

Lead Cross-Functional Teams Influence without direct authority in matrixed environments. Foster collaboration across diverse teams. Create accountability. Push the organization toward innovative, modern delivery practices—whether that's leveraging automation, new tools, or AI-enabled productivity solutions.

Contribute to Continuous Improvement Help the PMO evolve. Share lessons learned. Develop best practices and templates that make future programs stronger. Champion modern delivery methodologies and tools that improve how we work.


What you bring

Experience & Expertise — Must Have

  • 10+ years managing complex, client-facing programs—software implementations, business transformations, or large-scale delivery initiatives

  • Background in Benefits or Pension delivery, SaaS platforms, enterprise software implementation, or related complex environments

  • PMP certification (non-negotiable)

  • Proven success delivering large, multi-workstream programs with real business impact

  • Strong financial acumen: budgeting, forecasting, change control, risk management

  • Executive presence: you can speak confidently with senior leaders and negotiate across boundaries

  • Mastery of delivery tools: MS Project, Azure DevOps, Jira, Smartsheet, or similar platforms

  • Degree in Business, Technology, Engineering, Finance, Actuarial Science, or a related field

The Right Mindset

  • You thrive in client-facing environments and actually enjoy the complexity of stakeholder management

  • You balance strategic thinking with disciplined execution—you see the big picture and sweat the details

  • You influence teams across a matrixed org and make things happen without always having direct authority

  • You're comfortable with ambiguity but driven to create clarity and alignment

  • You see yourself as a trusted advisor, not just a program manager

Nice-to-Have Assets

  • Experience leading client migrations, platform modernizations, or large-scale transformation programs

  • Background specifically in Retirement, Pension, or Health & Welfare delivery

  • Agile, Scrum Master, Prosci, or related certifications

  • Track record of leveraging automation and AI tools to improve delivery efficiency and reporting

  • Experience in SaaS/cloud-based technology environments

Salary Range: $100,000 - $120,000

Actual total compensation will be determined based on factors such as knowledge, skills, performance and experience. We encourage all qualified candidates to apply, even if the posted salary range doesn't match your expectations. We're open to discussing competitive compensation packages tailored to your experience level and expertise.

TELUS Health offers rewarding benefits, which may vary per job function, such as:

  • Comprehensive total rewards package highlighting competitive salary and bonus structures, minimum 3 weeks of vacation, and flexible benefits plan to meet the needs of you and your family

  • Flexibility to work in-office, virtually or a combination of both

  • Generous company matched pension

  • Opportunity to give back to communities in which we work, live and serve

  • Career growth and learning & development opportunities to develop your skills

  • And much more…

Job Type: This is for a current vacancy.


Why this role, why now

You'll partner with executive clients on transformational work that matters. You'll grow your influence and strategic leadership in a high-performing PMO culture that values delivery excellence and innovation. You'll have flexibility in how you work, competitive compensation, and real opportunities to shape how we deliver for the future.

A bit about us

We’re a people-focused, customer-first, purpose-driven team who works together every day to innovate and do good. We improve lives through our technology solutions and foster a culture of innovation that empowers team members to solve complex problems and create remarkable human outcomes in a digital world.

TELUS is proud to foster an inclusive culture that embraces diversity. We are committed to fair employment practices and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment. We offer accommodation for applicants with disabilities, as required, during the recruitment process.

Note for Quebec candidates: if knowledge of English is required for this position, it is because the team member will be asked, on a regular basis, to interact in English with external or internal parties or to use English applications or software as part of their tasks.

By applying to this role, you understand and agree that your information will be shared with the TELUS Group of Companies’ Talent Acquisition team(s) and/or any leader(s) who will be part of the selection process.

title: HSE Specialist
description:
At ABB, we help industries run leaner and cleaner—and every person here makes that happen. You’ll be empowered to lead, supported to grow, and proud of the impact we create together. Join us and help run what runs the world.

This position reports to:

Business Manager - Operations

__

Your Role and Responsibilities

As an HSE Specialist, you play a crucial role in creating and maintaining a safe, healthy, and sustainable working environment at our Ede site. You are a trusted advisor, coach, and sparring partner for colleagues at all levels of the organization, helping to strengthen our health, safety, and environmental culture on a daily basis.

You combine strategic insight with a hands-on approach. One moment, you are working on compliance matters, reporting, or audits; the next, you are out on the shop floor supporting colleagues in working safely and improving processes. Through your expertise and persuasive communication skills, you increase awareness and drive sustainable improvements in health, safety, and environmental performance.

In this role, you will be responsible for:

  • Driving behavioral change and increasing awareness around health, safety, and environmental topics.
  • Ensuring compliance with legislation, regulations, policies, procedures, and certification requirements.
  • Implementing new legislation, internal directives, and HSE initiatives.
  • Coordinating and supporting internal and external audits, inspections, and compliance reviews.
  • Developing, maintaining, and improving HSE procedures, work instructions, and reporting.
  • Investigating incidents and initiating corrective and preventive actions.
  • Ensuring the availability of appropriate safety equipment, tools, and personal protective equipment.
  • Supporting HSE activities within both the manufacturing environment and commercial departments, including Sales.
  • Collaborating with national and international stakeholders to further strengthen ABB's HSE culture.
  • Initiating and supporting sustainability and circularity projects.

Your Team

You will join an engaged and collaborative organization where ownership, accountability, and continuous improvement are highly valued. Every workday starts with a stand-up meeting, ensuring everyone understands the priorities and how we can achieve our goals together.

The Ede site is characterized by an open and entrepreneurial culture where initiative is valued and employees are given the freedom to make an impact. In this role, you will work closely with colleagues from production, sales, management, and site leadership. As a result, you will have a visible presence throughout the organization and a direct influence on how health, safety, and environmental practices are embedded in daily operations.

More About ABB

ABB is a global technology leader in electrification and automation. With approximately 150,000 employees in more than 100 countries, we help our customers operate more efficiently, productively, and sustainably.

At our Ede facility, we manufacture high-quality plastic installation boxes and enclosures for residential and commercial construction applications. From this location, we make an important contribution to delivering safe and innovative electrical solutions.

Qualifications for the Role

You are an independent and proactive HSE professional who easily connects with people and can translate complex challenges into practical solutions. You are comfortable taking ownership, maintaining a visible presence on the shop floor, and engaging others in a positive way to embrace change.

Additionally, you bring:

  • Bachelor's degree level (HBO) working and thinking capability.
  • A completed Higher Safety Management (HVK) qualification.
  • At least 5 years of relevant experience in a similar role, such as HSE Specialist, Safety Advisor, or QHSE Manager.
  • Experience with ISO certifications and management systems.
  • Extensive experience in a manufacturing or industrial environment.
  • Knowledge of electrical engineering and NEN 3140 is a strong advantage.
  • The ability to translate legislation and regulations into concrete actions and implementation plans.

title: Senior ASIC Engineer - Post Silicon Validation
description:
The application window is expected to close on: 11/09/2026

Meet the Team:

The Silicon One team creates innovative hardware platforms central to the AI era, powering Cisco’s core Switching, Routing, and Wireless products for organizations globally. Our innovations in silicon, optics, and hardware platforms are shaping the technology industry. We're a global team of creative experts, bringing our unique backgrounds and bold ideas to push boundaries and help each other grow. Because full product development—from design to qualification to production—is within our team, we’re able to think differently, experiment more, and work quickly. Join us to power the future of the digital world.

Your Impact:

In this role as a Post-Silicon Validation Engineer, you will be responsible for:

  • Planning and setting up Silicon Bring-up infrastructure, including system boot, initialization, and Power-On of ASICs.

  • Working closely with design, verification, and board teams to root-cause and resolve functional and electrical issues.

  • Preparing the Validation Test plan and executing functional and performance testing targeting IP, Subsystem, and full-chip stress testing and corner case analysis.

  • Developing and extending post-silicon validation infrastructure, automation, and test suites, including implementing efficient result capture, analysis, and regression frameworks.

  • Applying expertise with lab instrumentation (oscilloscopes, analyzers, traffic generators) as part of validation and characterization.

  • Working closely with RTL, DFT, ATE, firmware, and system architecture teams to ensure a smooth transition from pre-silicon verification to post-silicon validation.

  • Providing critical feedback on test escapes, yield issues, and silicon errata, influencing silicon revisions and firmware/driver workarounds.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical or Computer Engineering and 7+ years experience; a Master's degree with 4+ years of experience; or a PhD with 1+ years of experience.

  • Prior experience in post-silicon validation, bring-up, and debug with ASICs.

  • Prior experience in early silicon bring-up, debug, and validation.

  • Prior experience bringing up standard peripheral interfaces (I2C, SPI, JTAG) and protocols (PCIe, Ethernet).

  • Prior experience working with firmware, bootloaders, and low-level silicon debug environments; fluency in C, Python, and scripting for validation automation.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with memory subsystems (HBM, DDR).

  • Electrical and thermal performance characterization activities.

  • System Verilog/UVM-based verification and emulation-based verification.

Why Cisco?

At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint.

Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere.

We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.

title: Account Payable Analyst
description:
Accounts Payable Analyst

AP & Treasury Coordinator

General Description

The Accounts Payable Analyst I is responsible for supporting accounts payable activities, ensuring timely and accurate processing of invoices, vendor records, payment documentation, and accounting transactions. The position provides administrative and operational support to the Finance team, helping maintain compliance with company policies, accounting requirements, and tax regulations while contributing to efficient financial operations.

Main Responsibilities

  • Support the processing and recording of vendor invoices in the ERP system.
  • Verify that invoices contain the required supporting documentation and approvals prior to processing.
  • Assist with vendor account maintenance, including new vendor setup and updates to vendor information.
  • Support weekly payment activities by preparing documentation and reports.
  • Respond to routine vendor inquiries regarding invoice and payment status, escalating complex issues when necessary.
  • Assist with vendor statement reconciliations and identification of discrepancies.
  • Support the preparation of accounting entries related to accounts payable transactions.
  • Monitor advance payments and follow up on supporting documentation as required.
  • Help maintain electronic accounting records and tax documentation, including payment receipts.
  • Assist in the preparation of month-end closing activities and supporting reconciliations.
  • Support BlackLine reconciliation processes and documentation requirements.
  • Maintain organized accounting records in accordance with company policies and audit requirements.
  • Support internal and external audit requests by gathering documentation and providing required information.
  • Assist with vendor portal administration, including user access requests and information updates.
  • Collaborate with internal departments to obtain information required for invoice processing and accrual activities.
  • Participate in process improvement initiatives and system implementation projects as assigned.

Required Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or related field.
  • 0-2 years of experience in Accounts Payable, Accounting, Finance, or internship/co-op experience in similar areas.
  • Basic understanding of accounting principles.
  • Experience using Microsoft Office applications, especially Excel.
  • Exposure to ERP systems is preferred but not required.
  • Knowledge of Mexican tax requirements is a plus.

Skills & Competencies

  • Intermediate English proficiency (written and spoken).
  • Basic to intermediate Microsoft Excel skills.
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Good organizational and time management skills.
  • Willingness to learn and develop accounting and finance knowledge.
  • Effective communication and teamwork skills.
  • Customer service orientation.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines.
  • Proactive attitude and continuous improvement mindset.
  • High level of integrity and confidentiality.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • Invoice processing accuracy.
  • Timely completion of assigned transactions.
  • Compliance with approval and documentation requirements.
  • Resolution time for vendor inquiries.
  • Reconciliation completion and accuracy.
  • Support provided during month-end close and audit activities.
